description: Full pipeline with 4 ensembles chained via graph: (1) ENUMERATE: Recon crew discovers target app boundaries, endpoints, tech stack, auth patterns. Currently Veritas-only — extend to work with ANY target (Juice Shop, VAmPI, internal apps). Outputs: app map, endpoint inventory, tech stack, auth flow. (2) SANDBOX SETUP: Provisions target environment. For external apps: docker compose profile rotation. For internal apps: LocalStack + CFN. Outputs: running target with health check. (3) CODE SCAN (SAST): New ensemble. Reads source code, analyzes for vuln patterns (IDOR, XSS, SQLi), outputs suspected locations with file/function/line + attack chains. Uses builder brick for internal code, http_request for open source. (4) PENTEST (DAST): Existing rt-scan-idor but made VULN-AGNOSTIC. Takes vuln_class as variable (IDOR, XSS, SQLi, SSRF). Skills/prompts/tools adjust based on vuln_class. Same best practices: multi-model ensemble, RAG from KB, evals after each run, games for reward signal. Each stage feeds the next via graph context. The full chain: enumerate → sandbox → code-scan → pentest → evals → games → blockchain → memory → loop.
title: EPIC: 4-Stage Security Pipeline — Enumerate → Sandbox → Code Scan → Pentest

description: Port A-MEM's self-evolving Zettelkasten pattern to the Neo4j memory adapter. When a new memory is stored: (1) find semantic neighbors via HNSW vector search, (2) run LLM analysis via llm_gateway to extract connections/tags/context updates, (3) update neighbor Memory nodes via Cypher. The evolution engine (evolution.py) is already backend-agnostic — it just needs a store that supports neighbor lookup and metadata updates. Neo4j is ideal because neighbor relationships become first-class graph edges (RELATED_TO, EVOLVED_FROM) instead of ChromaDB metadata. This keeps all memories, relationships, and evolution history in the same graph as security findings, events, experiments, and KB documents.
title: A-MEM evolution logic on Neo4j memory adapter

description:
Tenet violations found during the 3jcls architecture gate.

renderers-basic.tsx:61 (ButtonRenderer) and renderers-interactive.tsx:44 (FormRenderer) both call fetch('/api/tools/${tool}') directly, bypassing the BridgeAdapter seam that every other renderer hook uses (useToolData, useGraphData, ItemListRenderer, LazyTabContent, GraphViewerRenderer all go through useBridge).

Consequences:
1. Tenet 2/6 violation: the renderer package hardcodes a transport it is explicitly documented not to know about (bridge-adapter.ts docstring).
2. ~20 bricks already declare type:'form' with props.tool — including agent_agent_launch_swarm (agent/mcp/views.py:100) and memory_memory_retrieve. So a brick-declared view can ALREADY fire an operational tool. The epic premise 'clicking does nothing' is only true for Button-with-action; Form-with-tool is live.
3. These calls carry no envelope, no thread/run correlation, and never reach the chat transcript, so they produce divergent provenance from agent-fired calls.
4. props.tool vs A2UI catalog's props.action is already a forked naming for one concept.

Fix direction (per gate verdict): collapse both onto ONE dispatcher that routes through useBridge, and make the wire shape a typed ActionRef rather than a free-form tool string.
title: Arch: shared-renderer Button/Form bypass BridgeAdapter with raw fetch to /api/tools — ungated action path already shipped

acceptance_criteria: A human can discover and initiate any operational//authoring brick capability from the UI without typing in chat, using surfaces that add no persistent visual chrome. Human-initiated actions land in the same transcript and produce the same provenance as agent-initiated ones. ML tab pioneers the pattern and shows real data.
description:
Problem, stated precisely. Every brick has an MCP interface so an agent can drive it. The UI was built to DISPLAY what the agent was doing, so it has no verbs. Audit of the ML tab: 32 interactive elements, all of them navigation (11 top tabs, 5 sub-tabs) or drill-down (health chips, lineage rows, chevrons). Zero initiate work.

The Overview card says it outright: "Start the improvement loop - Create an immutable dataset artifact, train a model, evaluate it. Ask the assistant to run the relevant MCP operation." The UI instructs the human to leave the UI.

Key architectural finding that shapes the whole epic: the A2UI protocol ALREADY declares the interaction primitives. components/ui/src/factory/ui/runtime/a2ui/components.py:40-65 defines Button (optional prop "action"), Form (optional "action", "method", "submitLabel"), TextField, Select, DatePicker. But the only action handler in the frontend is chat/mcp-ui-frame.tsx:79 for the mcp-ui carrier. So bricks can already declare actions and nothing happens. This epic closes a loop that is half-built rather than inventing new architecture.

Design constraint that is not negotiable: the current aesthetic (minimal dark IDE surface, restrained palette, dense well-typed lists) is a feature. Every concept here is chosen because it adds ZERO persistent chrome - palettes are invisible until summoned, context menus attach to existing rows, empty states only occupy space when there is nothing else to show. No dashboards of buttons.

Second principle: one transcript. A human-fired action must appear in the chat rail as an activity message identical to an agent-fired one, carrying the same tool call and provenance. Otherwise the human path and agent path become two products that disagree.

Sequencing: bugs first (so screenshots we iterate on are honest), then the dispatcher (load-bearing for everything else), then palette, then contextual actions, then fork-a-run.
title: EPIC: human exploration surface — let a person drive the bricks, not just watch the agent

acceptance_criteria: A brick can declare a Button with an action in its views and clicking it invokes the named MCP tool with the declared arguments. Result refreshes the view. Failures surface as visible errors, never silently swallowed. An authoring-gated tool cannot be invoked from a view without passing the same gate the agent passes. Human-fired calls emit an activity message into the chat rail.
close_reason:
Implemented per the normative architecture-gate design (APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS).

Typed ActionRef: components/ui/src/factory/ui/runtime/a2ui/actions.py — frozen dataclass {brick, tool, args, arg_bindings, label, confirm, invalidates, idempotency_arg}. Validator rejects url/href/method/endpoint/uri/src/target/path (a view payload CANNOT name a non-MCP target), charset-locks brick+tool with re.fullmatch REJECT-not-coerce, constrains arg_bindings to the fixed $. grammar data_path already uses, and resolves the tool on the brick so a typo fails at ingestion. Form.method removed from the A2UI catalog.

One frontend dispatcher: useAction in frontends/shared-renderer/src/actions/. Routes through BridgeAdapter, surfaces pending/result/errors visibly. Both Button and Form use it.

Refresh: authoritative client refetch — useToolData registers into an invalidation registry, ActionRef.invalidates names the keys. The action response carries no view payload.

Idempotency: per-gesture UUID passed only when idempotency_arg is declared AND present in the target tool's schema; otherwise documented as at-most-once-per-gesture (in-flight dedupe on (tool, resolved args) + disabled control), NOT idempotent.

Policy-gate site: _authorize() in components/ui/src/factory/ui/mcp/action_dispatch.py — one function, one edit, because all dispatch funnels through ui_dispatch_action. Authz gate + loopback bind descoped by the user; the AC clause about @authoring parity is deferred with that descoping.

Anti-drift: (1) test_action_dispatch_real.py drives real bricks through the real bridge route and real aggregator, zero mocks; (2) test_action_ingestion_real_views.py walks every *_get_views in the repo; (3) action-fetch-canary.test.ts greps for the regression; (4) dispatcher-canary.test.tsx extended with SDK-verified transcript parity.

Verified end-to-end in the live browser: one POST to ui_dispatch_action, real result rendered, human tool call rode the next /run body.

Guardian: import_integrity PASS, bricks_index PASS, file_sizes 64 = exact baseline, zero new. Follow-ups filed: python-factory-9ha4d (durable transcript), python-factory-znoc5 (pre-existing Strands test drift).
description:
This is the load-bearing seam. The palette, contextual row actions and fork-a-run all sit on top of it. Build it first and build it right.

Current state: the protocol declares the primitives, the frontend ignores them.
- components/ui/src/factory/ui/runtime/a2ui/components.py:40-65 - Button has optional prop "action"; Form has "action", "method", "submitLabel"; TextField/Select/DatePicker exist.
- components/ui/src/factory/ui/runtime/models.py:169 serializes "action".
- The only action handler in the frontend is components/chat/mcp-ui-frame.tsx:79, scoped to the mcp-ui carrier.

So bricks can declare actions today and clicking does nothing. Close that loop.

Design questions for the architecture gate, NOT to be decided unilaterally by the implementer:
1. What is the wire shape of an action? Prefer a typed reference to an MCP tool plus argument bindings over a free-form string. It must be impossible for a view payload to name an arbitrary HTTP endpoint.
2. Authorization. @authoring tools are gated for the agent. A view-declared action must not become a bypass. Where does the gate live?
3. Argument binding. How does a row-scoped action bind the row's identity into arguments without the brick hand-writing per-row payloads?
4. Optimistic vs. authoritative refresh - does the action response carry a new view payload, or does the client re-fetch?
5. Idempotency for operational tools that spawn jobs, so a double-click cannot start two training runs.

Explicit non-goal: do not add a bespoke RPC layer. Everything routes through the existing MCP surface, because that is what keeps the human path and the agent path identical.

Lesson to carry from the dataset//ml//evals audit (epic python-factory-wvkvg): do not validate this against a mock of the tool layer. Test it against a real brick tool call. Two of the worst findings in that audit were adapters that passed tests because the test mocked the thing being integrated.
title: ui: frontend action dispatcher — wire A2UI Button.action/Form.action to call_brick_tool

description:
The highest-leverage concept in the epic, and the one that preserves the aesthetic best, because it is invisible until summoned.

You have ~689 tools across 40 bricks, each already carrying a name, a human description and a JSON input schema, discoverable via get_brick_tools. That is a complete command registry that nobody has to hand-maintain. VS Code exposes thousands of commands through exactly this affordance with no visual weight.

Requirements:
- Generate entries from the MCP tool schemas at runtime. Never hardcode a tool list - that is the mistake the evals brick made with its evaluator registry (three hand-synced literals, see python-factory-wvkvg.22).
- Scope to @operational and @authoring. @deterministic reads are not commands a human needs to fire.
- Order results with the active tab's brick first, then everything else, so the ML tab surfaces ML verbs without hiding the rest.
- Render the argument form from the tool's JSON schema. Required fields required, enums as selects, defaults prefilled.
- Show the resolved MCP call before submit so the human can see exactly what will run. This doubles as the teaching surface - it shows people what to ask the agent for.
- Progressive discovery caveat: list_bricks only reports loaded bricks and tools_count -1 means not yet loaded. The palette must trigger loading rather than showing an empty or partial registry.

Note python-factory-wvkvg.15 - the dataset brick is currently absent from MCP_INCLUDE_BRICKS, so its tools will not appear until that is fixed. Related but separately tracked.
title: ui: command palette generated from MCP tool schemas (Cmd-K)

description:
Depends on the action dispatcher (3jcls.3).

The Experiments sub-tab rows are already ideal anchors - clean single-line rows with a status pill, score, delta and chevron. Attach verbs to the object under the cursor: Re-run, Compare to..., Promote, Train challenger.

Why this shape: the affordance costs no permanent furniture, and it is IDE-native (a context menu is the most familiar exploration gesture in an editor). It also scales per object type without any new layout.

Implementation direction: bricks declare, per view row type, which tools apply and how the row's identity binds into the tool arguments. The frontend renders whatever the brick declares. Do not hardcode an ML-specific action list in React - that would fork the registry the same way the evaluator catalog did.

Accessibility: hover-only reveal is not sufficient. Actions must be reachable by keyboard on the focused row, and the context menu must be operable without a mouse.
title: ui: contextual actions on existing rows (hover//context menu)

acceptance_criteria: From any past training run, Fork produces an editable copy of its exact config with changed fields diff-highlighted against the parent. Submit creates a child run linked to the parent in lineage. The Lineage view shows the resulting tree, not a flat list. The composed call is inspectable and copyable as an MCP invocation.
description:
Depends on the action dispatcher (3jcls.3). This is the ML-specific concept the tab pioneers.

Rationale: nobody explores ML by filling in a blank training form. They take a run that worked and change two things. The exploratory primitive is therefore MUTATION OF A KNOWN-GOOD CONFIG, not creation from zero.

Design:
- Click a past run, hit Fork, get its full resolved config as an editable param set.
- Diff-highlight every field the human changes against the parent's value, so the experiment's intent is legible at a glance.
- Submit spawns a child run recorded as a child of the parent in lineage - the brick already models lineage, so the tree is mostly a rendering question.
- Show the composed MCP call, copyable, so the human can hand it to the agent or script it.

Two properties make this worth building over a generic form: the human never starts from nothing, and the artifact produced is a DIFF, which turns the Lineage tab into a real experiment tree instead of the flat receipt list it shows today.

Ties into the audit epic: forking preserves provenance by construction, which is exactly what python-factory-wvkvg.24 says is missing today (ten timeseries paths take bare URIs with no digest or manifest validation). A fork should carry the parent's dataset digest forward, not re-resolve a bare path.
title: ui: fork-a-run composer — explore ML by mutating a known-good config

description:
The principle that keeps this from becoming two products.

If a human fires ml_train_timeseries from the palette and the agent fires the same tool a minute later, both must appear in the chat rail as the same kind of activity message, with the same arguments and provenance. The only difference should be the actor.

Why it matters beyond tidiness:
- The agent needs to know what the human just did, or it will give stale advice and duplicate work. A shared transcript is the cheapest possible shared state.
- It makes the UI teach. A human who fires a palette command sees the exact call appear in the rail, which is the thing they would otherwise have had to know how to ask for.
- It prevents the audit failure mode at the UX layer: two paths to the same capability that drift apart because only one is exercised.

CopilotKit already ships activity messages and the chat surface already renders tool cards, so this is wiring rather than new machinery. Confirm against the installed dispatcher (frontends/next-dashboard/node_modules/@copilotkit/react-core/dist/) rather than assuming - SDK-first per repo tenets.
title: ui: human-fired actions must land in the same transcript as agent-fired ones

Strands/meta-arch consults from sopw still apply (same bug surface, same SDK-First documented gap). Files: frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/inspector-attach-workaround.tsx
description:
## Symptom

After the user clicks the inspector icon to open the window, then closes
the window via the "Close Web Inspector" X button (or the SDK assigning
`isOpen = false`), the `<cpk-web-inspector>` element re-renders with an
inline `transform: translate3d(1402.4px, 16px, 0px)`. With the parent
`.copilot-status-host` wrapper at `transform: scale(0.45)` (defined in
`frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/inspector.css`), the icon's
post-transform viewport position becomes:

  parent_rect.x + (translateX * 0.45) = 1303 + 631.08 = 1934.3

at viewport width 1440, i.e. the icon is rendered offscreen (right of
the viewport) and is unreachable by the mouse.

This reproduces the user-reported "Close inspector -> icon disappears /
can't reopen" bug that bd:python-factory-sopw's workaround was intended
to mitigate. The workaround only handles the persisted offscreen-
position case (pruneOffscreenIconPosition() reads
`localStorage['cpk:inspector:state'].customPosition.button`). It does
NOT handle the SDK's runtime-applied `transform: translate3d(...)` on
the host that fires AFTER `isOpen = false` because the SDK computes the
right-anchor relative to `window.innerWidth` and does not know about
the scale-0.45 wrapper context bd:python-factory-r8o7 introduced.

## Repro (verified via Playwright headless 2026-05-28)

1. localStorage.clear() and reload http://localhost:3000.
2. Wait for cpk-web-inspector to mount.
   el.shadowRoot.querySelector('button.console-button').getBoundingClientRect()
   -> x=1303, y=877 (in viewport).
   el.getAttribute('style') -> "position: relative; transform: none; ...".
3. Click button.console-button -> el.isOpen === true.
4. Click button[aria-label="Close Web Inspector"] -> el.isOpen === false.
5. Re-read button rect -> x=1934, y=884 (offscreen).
   el.getAttribute('style') ->
   "position: relative; inset: auto; z-index: 50;
    transform: translate3d(1402.4px, 16px, 0px);"

## Severity

P1. Once the icon is hidden offscreen, the only way to access the
inspector is a localStorage clear + reload. This breaks the second of
the two regressions bd-sopw was filed to fix. The first regression
(subscriber teardown after drag/dock-toggle) is genuinely fixed by
the new MutationObserver-based workaround - verified end-to-end with
3 back-to-back synthetic remount cycles + a fresh chat run that
produced a full RUN_STARTED -> REASONING -> TEXT -> RUN_FINISHED event
sequence on AG-UI Events.

## Likely fix paths (read-only QA, not prescribing)

1. Pin the host's transform on close. The inspector-attach-
   workaround.tsx MutationObserver could detect the post-close
   transform and override it (e.g. style.transform = 'none' when the
   element is icon-mode and inside .copilot-status-host). Cheap,
   surgical, removable when upstream patches.
2. Ditch the scaled-wrapper layout. inspector.css reparents the
   inspector into a 24px footer slot via transform: scale(0.45). A
   non-transform-based scaling (e.g. CSS zoom or rendering a custom
   24px button that proxies el.click() via portals) sidesteps the
   SDK's viewport-anchor math entirely. Heavier change.
3. Upstream: the SDK's runtime auto-positioning should query the
   nearest containing block, not window.innerWidth, when computing
   anchor offsets. File against @copilotkitnext/react.

## Acceptance

After open -> close cycle on a fresh dashboard load, the icon's
getBoundingClientRect() must satisfy
rect.x + rect.width <= window.innerWidth && rect.y + rect.height <=
window.innerHeight. Verifiable via Playwright probe identical to the
repro above.

## Files involved (read-only context)

- frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/inspector-attach-workaround.tsx
  (workaround scope; currently only prunes localStorage, not runtime style)
- frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/inspector.css
  (parent transform scale(0.45) - bd:python-factory-r8o7)
- frontends/next-dashboard/components/layout/copilot-status-item.tsx
  (mounts inspector inside .copilot-status-host)
- @copilotkitnext/[email protected] dist/index.mjs
  (SDK auto-positioning logic, runtime-applied translate)

## Tenet

dev-principles.md SDK-First "build it AND document the gap": the
existing workaround docstring already cites the SDK lifecycle bugs;
adding a runtime-style override for the host transform fits the same
scope and stays removable when the upstream layout-aware patch lands.
title: Bug: Inspector icon renders offscreen after open->close cycle (.copilot-status-host scale(0.45) + SDK translate3d)

close_reason: Implemented: CWE-639 equivalence fix + hybrid scoring (deterministic + Strands LLM eval). 18 tests passing.
description: The gt_benchmark MCP gt_score tool uses strict deterministic matching (file + line + CWE exact match). This fails on real-world scenarios where: (1) CWE hierarchies matter (CWE-639 is a child of CWE-863 but scores as a miss), (2) findings point to different layers of the same bug (VetsController.java vs VetClinicsPageController.java), (3) semantic similarity matters more than string equality. Proposal: pair the deterministic gt_score with Strands LLM evaluators (faithfulness, response_relevance, output) to produce a hybrid score. The deterministic pass gives P/R/F1 on exact matches; the LLM eval pass scores semantic closeness for near-misses. Together they answer: did the tool find what's in the GT DB, and how close did it get? Discovered during PenPal vs Shepherd GT comparison where Finding #1 (VetsController IDOR) was clearly the same bug family as the GT (VetClinicsPageController IDOR, CWE-639) but scored 0/0/0 on all deterministic modes.
title: GT Benchmark: hybrid scoring — deterministic gt_score + Strands LLM evals for fuzzy matching

description:
REPRO: curl localhost:8000/ag-ui/run with same threadId twice. Msg1: full text deltas. Msg2+: only RUN_STARTED + RUN_FINISHED, ~2.2s latency.

ROOT CAUSE: components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_chat.py:170-176

In stream() finally, agent.cancel() is called UNCONDITIONALLY (even on clean producer completion). agent.cancel() sets Strands' Agent._cancel_signal (agent.py:400). Strands clears _cancel_signal inside stream_async's own try/finally (agent.py:878), but the adapter sets it AFTER that finally already ran. So the signal sticks on the cached per-thread Agent.

On next stream(): stream_async runs, model emits first chunk, process_stream (streaming.py:418) sees cancel_signal.is_set() and yields ModelStopReason(stop_reason=cancelled) which has is_callback_event=False, so no deltas fire. Producer drains zero events; SSE only emits RUN_STARTED + RUN_FINISHED.

stream_async's own finally then clears the signal, but the adapter's finally re-sets it. Forever.

EVIDENCE:
- /tmp/qa-msg1.txt: 116 lines of TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT deltas
- /tmp/qa-msg2.txt, /tmp/qa-fresh2.txt, /tmp/qa-fresh3.txt: 4 lines each (RUN_STARTED + RUN_FINISHED only)
- New threadId works first call, breaks from second call onward (same pattern)

NOT THE CAUSE:
- python-factory-l6ya (invocation lock): msg2 returns 200 not ConcurrencyException; lock IS released cleanly by stream_async's finally
- Cache pollution: bridge.detach() correctly clears queue/loop slots
- Model/creds: fresh threadId works

FIX SHAPE: only call agent.cancel() when producer is still running. Or, after cancel, also clear agent._cancel_signal as defence-in-depth.

REGRESSION TEST: integration test that drives stream() twice on the same thread_id and asserts both invocations yield non-empty TextDeltaEvent stream.

DEPENDS_ON_MEMORY: fc3b6bed-1997-4428-a17f-ee9639a0cc44, 228dc0be-3873-49ae-9a39-21590700cada
title: Chat: 2nd+ messages on same thread return empty SSE — agent.cancel() in finally poisons next invocation

description: ROOT CAUSE: DiskRegistryStore.save_persona writes <id>.yaml (registry_store.py line 67-71). On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS default, Windows NTFS) two persona ids differing ONLY by case (e.g. MyAgent vs myagent, or unicode U+0162 vs U+0163) map to the SAME file, so the second save silently OVERWRITES the first. InMemoryRegistryStore keys an exact dict (registry_store.py line 96-99) and keeps BOTH. The two RegistryStore adapters are therefore NOT behaviorally equivalent on case-only-differing ids. IMPACT: low-moderate. _ID_RE (authoring/validation.py line 16) accepts mixed case, so a user CAN author MyAgent then myagent; on macOS/Windows the first persona vanishes silently on reload. Built-ins are unaffected (all lowercase, merge collision is exact/case-sensitive and correct). REPRO deterministic on macOS: DiskRegistryStore save MyAgent then save myagent, load_personas returns only [myagent], MyAgent LOST. ALSO BREAKS the implementer Phase 0 test test_unified_registry_properties.py::test_disk_and_memory_stores_agree (line 105) because its _id_strategy (line 28-33) uses whitelist_categories L,N including cased unicode. SUGGESTED FIX (meta-architect call, touches RegistryStore Protocol case-equivalence semantics): (a) case-safe disk stem, or (b) reject case-collision on save / in _ID_RE, or (c) constrain that test strategy to a case-stable alphabet AND document the disk case-fold caveat in adapter docstring + ports.py. description:
Pre-existing bug (predates and is unrelated to the McpError->MCPError rename in GH issue #746). CatalogTool (components/mcp_utils/src/factory/mcp_utils/runtime/catalog_models.py) is a plain frozen dataclass with only name/description/fn -- it has NO .run() method. The real invocation path is ToolCatalog.call_tool(name, arguments) (async), which wraps invoke_native_tool and returns a native CallToolResult.

Dozens of test files across many bricks still call tool.run(arguments) or tool.run({...}) expecting the old FastMCP-era Tool.run() API (e.g. components/oracle/test/factory/oracle/test_mcp_contract.py, components/http_client/test/factory/http_client/test_mcp_contract.py, components/logger/test/factory/logger/test_mcp_contract.py, components/notification/test/factory/notification/test_typed_mcp_boundary.py, components/machine_learning/test/factory/machine_learning/test_can_model_config_preflight.py, components/machine_learning/test/factory/machine_learning/test_can_evaluation_persistence_roundtrip.py, components/machine_learning/test/factory/machine_learning/test_timeseries_model_config_mcp.py, components/evals/test/factory/evals/test_selected_typed_mcp.py, components/evals/test/factory/evals/test_ui_explorer_typed_mcp.py, components/payments/test/factory/payments/test_mcp_contract.py -- there are more, this is not exhaustive).

Confirmed via git stash that these failures exist identically on unmodified main -- this is not something my McpError-rename edits introduced.

Fix options:
1. Add a .run(arguments) compatibility shim to CatalogTool that delegates to the owning ToolCatalog.call_tool (requires CatalogTool to know its catalog, or a free helper function).
2. Update every failing test call site from tool.run(arguments) to catalog.call_tool(name, arguments) (matches the pattern already used correctly by components/agent, components/dataset, components/workflow, components/permissions tests).
Option 2 matches the already-correct pattern used elsewhere and avoids adding surface area to the immutable CatalogTool dataclass. Needs a sweep across all affected bricks; scope it as a discovered task with sub-tasks per brick if large.
title: Bug: CatalogTool has no .run() method used by many typed MCP contract tests

close_reason: Fixed in PR #588 — strands_mcp_chat.py stream() finally no longer calls agent.cancel(); uses producer.cancel() which lets stream_async clear _cancel_signal naturally (memory 6dc45819 cited in source comment lines 178-181)
description:
REPRO: curl localhost:8000/ag-ui/run with same threadId twice. Msg1: full text deltas. Msg2+: only RUN_STARTED + RUN_FINISHED, ~2.2s latency.

ROOT CAUSE: components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_chat.py:170-176

In stream() finally, agent.cancel() is called UNCONDITIONALLY (even on clean producer completion). agent.cancel() sets Strands' Agent._cancel_signal (agent.py:400). Strands clears _cancel_signal inside stream_async's own try/finally (agent.py:878), but the adapter sets it AFTER that finally already ran. So the signal sticks on the cached per-thread Agent.

On next stream(): stream_async runs, model emits first chunk, process_stream (streaming.py:418) sees cancel_signal.is_set() and yields ModelStopReason(stop_reason=cancelled) which has is_callback_event=False, so no deltas fire. Producer drains zero events; SSE only emits RUN_STARTED + RUN_FINISHED.

stream_async's own finally then clears the signal, but the adapter's finally re-sets it. Forever.

EVIDENCE:
- /tmp/qa-msg1.txt: 116 lines of TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT deltas
- /tmp/qa-msg2.txt, /tmp/qa-fresh2.txt, /tmp/qa-fresh3.txt: 4 lines each (RUN_STARTED + RUN_FINISHED only)
- New threadId works first call, breaks from second call onward (same pattern)

NOT THE CAUSE:
- python-factory-l6ya (invocation lock): msg2 returns 200 not ConcurrencyException; lock IS released cleanly by stream_async's finally
- Cache pollution: bridge.detach() correctly clears queue/loop slots
- Model/creds: fresh threadId works

FIX SHAPE: only call agent.cancel() when producer is still running. Or, after cancel, also clear agent._cancel_signal as defence-in-depth.

REGRESSION TEST: integration test that drives stream() twice on the same thread_id and asserts both invocations yield non-empty TextDeltaEvent stream.

description: DISCOVERED while debugging bd-gzqt. The hatch-polylith-bricks editable wheel COPIES brick source files into .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/factory/* rather than symlinking. Every brick edit creates drift between source and the snapshot. Affected: any process launched WITHOUT PYTHONPATH=bases/*/src:components/*/src (notably the kiroPowers companion-x power, which Kiro spawns from the installed mcp.json without that env). Concrete failure mode this session: bd-u3xy LearningRecallPlugin + bd-o7t8 learning.applied emit + bd-vfgf FileSessionManager + bd-kq6u workflow.improvement handler all landed correctly in source, but kiroPowers companion-x continued running pre-fix code from site-packages. Required uv sync --reinstall-package python-factory to refresh. PROPOSED FIX: update .kiro/powers/installed/companion-x/mcp.json + repo source at ~/.kiro/powers/repos/companion-x/mcp.json to inject PYTHONPATH=bases/api/src:bases/mcp_server/src:bases/worker/src:bases/blueprint/src:components/agent/src:components/memory/src:components/events/src:...:components/games/src in the env so source always wins over snapshot. Same approach the local API uses. Long-term: file an issue against hatch-polylith-bricks for true editable mode (PEP 660 file-as-symlink), or add a custom .pth that prepends source paths. Discovered-from python-factory-gzqt.
title: Polylith editable-install drift: Kiro power launches without PYTHONPATH, loads stale factory/* from site-packages

description:
Found while running the architecture gate for the human-exploration epic. Verified on this machine, not inferred.

1. POST /api/tools/{tool_name} invokes ANY aggregator tool from an unauthenticated JSON body. Verified:
     curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/tools/cache_health_check -d '{}'  ->  HTTP 200 with real result
   bases/api/runtime/bridge.py::execute_tool calls _extract_envelope, which returns None when there is no Bearer token, and then proceeds to _call_tool anyway.

2. /api/health reports total_tools: 689. All of them are reachable this way, including @authoring tools (persona create/delete, config mutation) and cost-bearing operational ones (agent_agent_launch_swarm, sandbox Docker provisioning, ledger writes).

3. _mcp_category is metadata only - zero production readers across components/ and bases/ (the single grep hit is a comment at agent/runtime/models.py:59). So the @authoring marker enforces nothing. There is no gate to bypass; the gate does not exist. Tracked in detail as python-factory-p9b98.

4. The acute part: bases/api/main.py:60 defaults FACTORY_API_HOST to 0.0.0.0, and lsof confirms the listener is TCP *:8000, i.e. all interfaces rather than loopback. On any shared network the whole tool surface is reachable by anyone who can route to the host. scripts/companion-x-ui.sh sets no host override, so the normal local dev path is the exposed path.

Mitigating factor, verified by reading rather than probing: strands_tools shell and python_repl are attached to the CHAT PERSONA (agent/runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_chat_persona.py:107-135), not registered into the aggregator's tool registry. The op_kind_lookup seed entries for them exist so the chat adapter can stamp opKind on the terminal-mirror wire. So this is not unauthenticated remote command execution via the gateway. I did not probe POST /api/tools/shell to confirm the 404.

Immediate mitigation, no code change: export FACTORY_API_HOST=127.0.0.1 before running scripts/companion-x-ui.sh.

Why P0 relative to the rest of the epic: the human-exploration work adds first-class UI affordances on top of this exact invocation path. Widening a path that has no gate is the wrong order. python-factory-p9b98 and this bead must land before python-factory-3jcls.3.
title: SECURITY: API exposes 689 unauthenticated tool-invocation endpoints on 0.0.0.0

description: Article reference: 'Stop AI Agent Hallucinations' by Elizabeth Fuentes (the-article.md). Technique 2: Semantic Tool Selection. WHAT: Replace the static ALLOWED_BRICK_PREFIXES filter in components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/tools.py with per-query semantic filtering using Neo4j HNSW vector indexes. Currently every query gets the same ~50 tools regardless of intent. Paper shows 86.4% error reduction and 89% token savings with semantic filtering. WHY: With 300+ MCP tools, the chat agent wastes tokens and makes more selection errors. A security question should get security tools, an ML question should get ML tools. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) At agent startup or tool registry change, create ToolDescription nodes in Neo4j with name, description, brick prefix. Embed descriptions via existing embedder. Create vector index 'tool_descriptions'. (2) In select_tools(), embed the user query, run graph_vector_search against tool_descriptions index, return top-k (e.g. 10-15) most relevant tools. (3) Fallback: if Neo4j unavailable, fall back to current static prefix filtering. (4) Use existing graph brick infrastructure — graph_create_vector_index, graph_set_embedding, graph_vector_search — no FAISS dependency needed. FILES: components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/tools.py (main change), components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/chat.py (pass query to select_tools), components/agent/src/factory/agent/mcp/tools.py (_build_chat_tools passes query). BENEFITS FOR KIRO: When Kiro talks through Companion-X via agent_reason, the chat agent gets semantically filtered tools. Running Companion-X as MCP backend for any project means both Kiro and chat agent benefit.
title: Semantic tool selection: replace static prefix filtering with per-query Neo4j vector search

description:
Kiro session (2026-07-23) recommendation. See addendum in
`.github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md` and the Session Resume
entry in `.agents/steering/can-failure-prediction.md` (2026-07-23) for
full context and the field-research basis for this recommendation.

## Problem

Current `failure_injection.py`
(`components/dataset/src/factory/dataset/runtime/adapters/failure_injection.py`)
has 8 modes but most mutate a single signal in isolation (drop_to_zero,
signal_freeze, spike_noise, signal_drift, sensor_degradation). Real
faults usually manifest as a coordinated shift across multiple
correlated signals (e.g. coolant_temp rising + fan_rpm rising +
engine_load rising together), not one signal going to zero. This is
the leading theory (per `can-failure-prediction-review.md` and current
weak-supervision literature) for why AUROC 0.97-1.00 is inflated: the
model is likely learning to detect the injection method, not a real
failure signature. `correlation_break` is the closest existing mode to
"realistic" but only swaps two signals' values rather than modeling a
coordinated, physically-plausible shift.

This is decoupled from and does NOT need to wait on the real-label
validation work in `sbhyq.1` (which is blocked on external data
access) -- it is a pure engineering improvement to the existing
rule-based injector and can proceed now, independently.

## Work

1. Use the correlation matrix already computed by `can_profile.py` to
   identify signal clusters that move together.
2. Add a new failure mode (or extend `correlation_break`) that shifts
   a whole correlated cluster together in a physically consistent
   direction/magnitude, rather than single-signal drift/zero/freeze.
3. Constrain injected trajectories to the rate-of-change / delta
   thresholds `can_profile.py` already computes, so drift/spikes never
   exceed physically plausible slew rates for that signal.
4. Replace hard on/off failure-window label flips with a ramped
   onset/decay (gradual severity increase then decrease) instead of an
   instant `is_failure=1` window.
5. Reweight `failure_modes` defaults so multi-signal/correlated modes
   are the primary training signal and single-signal modes
   (drop_to_zero, signal_freeze, spike_noise) are documented as weaker
   positive controls, not primary signal -- this is a config/default
   change, not new injection code, per
   `can-failure-prediction-review.md` section 9.1 step 3.

## Acceptance

- New/extended correlated injection mode covers >=2 correlated signals
  per event, magnitude/direction consistent with the correlation sign.
- Injected deltas never exceed `can_profile`'s measured max
  rate-of-change for that signal (physical plausibility check,
  testable).
- Failure severity ramps in/out over the event window rather than an
  instant flip.
- `can_synthesize` default `failure_modes` weighting documented and
  updated to favor correlated modes.
- Existing failure_injection tests (`test_can_failure_modes.py`,
  `test_can_synthesize.py`) updated/extended, still green.
title: Physics-constrained correlated multi-signal failure injection

description: The Companion-X IDE panels render the same brick views as the Web dashboard via @companion-x/shared-renderer, but they look RAW (plain cards/tabs/badges, no spacing/color). Root cause (confirmed): shared-renderer components are styled with Tailwind utility classes (grep: 167 text-, 58 flex, 37 gap-, 27 bg-, 25 rounded, px-/py-/grid/...) + vendored shadcn primitives. In next-dashboard these compile via Tailwind v4 (globals.css @import tailwindcss + content scanning) into the served CSS. In the Theia browser-app there is NO Tailwind/PostCSS build and shared-renderer ships NO compiled CSS, so the utility classes resolve to nothing → unstyled. FIX OPTIONS (needs a small design decision — Tailwind pipeline for a shared React package consumed by TWO bundlers, Next/SWC + Theia/esbuild): (a) ship a precompiled stylesheet from shared-renderer (Tailwind CLI scanning its own src, emit lib/styles.css) and import it in the panels extension / browser-app; (b) add a Tailwind/PostCSS step to the Theia browser-app esbuild over the shared-renderer classes; (c) vendor a static CSS. Option (a) is likely cleanest (build-once in the package, both consumers import). Also feed manifest accent colors (Track 10 ht2gq, deferred) once styled. This is the 'beautification' baseline — fixing it makes panels look ~80% as polished as the Web dashboard before any custom UX work; the richer animation-forward pass (north star #5) is a later dedicated ux-designer effort. Scope: frontends/shared-renderer + frontends/theia-ide (browser-app + panels). Discovered during epic ons71 panel bring-up. NOT functionally blocking.

description: Article reference: 'Stop AI Agent Hallucinations' by Elizabeth Fuentes (the-article.md). Technique 1: Graph-RAG. WHAT: Add automatic entity/relationship extraction during kb_ingest when Neo4j is the backend. Currently KB's Neo4j adapter (components/kb/src/factory/kb/runtime/retrieval/neo4j_vector.py) stores flat KBDocument nodes with embeddings. Need to extract entities and relationships from ingested text and write them as proper graph nodes/edges. WHY: Enables Text2Cypher pattern — LLM writes Cypher queries for aggregation/counting/relationship questions instead of guessing from vector chunks. Paper shows RAG fabricates statistics while Graph-RAG computes exact answers. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) Add neo4j-graphrag as optional pip dep of KB brick's neo4j adapter. (2) Add extract_entities option to Neo4jVectorStore.add() — when True, run LLM-driven entity/relationship extraction via neo4j-graphrag after storing the document. Extracted entities go into Neo4j as proper graph nodes with relationships. (3) Add routing guidance to chat agent system prompt: for aggregation/counting/relationship queries, prefer graph_query with Cypher over kb_search. (4) Default extract_entities=True when backend is neo4j. FILES: components/kb/src/factory/kb/runtime/retrieval/neo4j_vector.py (add extraction), components/kb/BRICK.yaml (add neo4j-graphrag dep), components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/ (routing guidance). REFERENCE: cognee memory adapter already does entity extraction — similar pattern.
title: Graph-RAG: KG construction pipeline in KB brick Neo4j adapter

description: Discovered while fixing chat workflow streaming (python-factory-anci). invoke_graph_async (components/agent/mcp/async_tools.py) spawns python -m factory.agent.scripts.run_graph via subprocess.Popen. The child has its own mcp_utils.event_bus._subscribers (process-local). Events emitted by the child's GraphLifecyclePlugin/executor never reach the parent's event_bus, so AG-UI streaming will not light up for graph workflows even after phase 1 is wired. Plan (meta-architect approved): stdout sentinel — child print(json.dumps({sentinel,event})) per event, parent _monitor thread reads proc.stdout line-by-line and republishes via events_publish on parent runtime. Preferred over status-file because zero new infra and same loss profile in practice.
title: Phase 2: Forward subprocess events from invoke_graph_async to parent event_bus

- Strands ReasoningTextStreamEvent dict shape: {reasoningText, delta, reasoning: True}
- All providers (Anthropic native + Bedrock Converse + LiteLLM + OpenAI Responses + Z.AI GLM5) funnel through the SAME shape
- Ollama emits silent (no reasoning events) — non-reasoning model
- ChatStreamEvent.ReasoningTextEvent already exists (components/agent/runtime/models.py:73)
- strands_mcp_chat_stream.py:81-82 already emits ReasoningTextEvent correctly

description:
phx2m R2 E2E canary BLOCK. PR #609 (commit 2f7bc7b0) shipped `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` with no nonce/hash strategy. The unit test in `lib/security/__tests__/csp.test.ts` even asserts `'unsafe-inline'` is forbidden. But Next.js App Router emits ~13 inline scripts on every page load — `__next_f.push([1,'7:I[...']` RSC streaming chunks plus dev-mode React Refresh runtime — and these have no nonce and no precomputed hash in the directive. Result: every inline script is blocked, React fibers never attach (`__reactContainer$`/`__reactFiber$` keys absent on body children and on the send button), CopilotKit can't bind to its provider, the status bar reports "Disconnected", and the send-message button stays `disabled` even when the textarea has text. The chat surface is functionally dead.

EVIDENCE (collected via playwright power against http://localhost:3000):

1) HEADERS PRESENT — `fetch('/', {method:'HEAD'})` returns CSP + X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN + COOP same-origin + COEP credentialless + Permissions-Policy + Referrer-Policy. Header wiring works; the directive shape is the problem.

2) CSP RUNTIME ERRORS — console:
   - 13 "Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval''" blocks (one per inline script with sha256 hash).
   - "Evaluating a string as JavaScript violates the following Content Security Policy directive because 'unsafe-eval' is not an allowed source of script" from @next/react-refresh-utils/dist/runtime.js (dev-mode HMR).
   - "Connecting to 'http://localhost:8000/health' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: 'connect-src 'self' https: wss:'" — useHealth poll to the absolute API_URL fails. Today /api/health works through the proxy route, but http://localhost:8000 is a valid configured API_URL.

3) REACT NOT HYDRATED — `Object.keys(document.body.firstChild)` shows zero React fiber/container keys. `document.querySelector('[data-testid=copilot-send-button]')` exists in the SSR HTML but is not React-bound, `btn.disabled === true`, `btn.click()` is a no-op.

4) STATUS BAR DISCONNECTED — useHealth never fires because React doesn't hydrate.

5) CHAT FLOW IMPOSSIBLE — Tried filling the textarea, Enter, button click, native HTMLTextAreaElement.value setter + synthetic input event. Send button stays disabled. Zero `[data-message-role]` messages ever attach.

ROOT CAUSE: lib/security/csp.ts directives are mutually exclusive with Next.js App Router runtime. `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` does not cover Next inline RSC scripts or React Refresh `new Function`.

NEXT.JS COMPATIBLE FIX:
- App Router needs middleware-injected `script-src 'nonce-<random>' 'strict-dynamic'` with the nonce mirrored to <script nonce={nonce}> server-side via `headers()`/`cookies()`. See nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/configuring/content-security-policy.
- Alternatively guard `buildSecurityHeaders()` so dev mode (`process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`) appends `'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline'` for script-src; production swaps to nonce. Either way the test in csp.test.ts that forbids 'unsafe-inline' must be split into prod/dev variants.

REPRO:
1. `cd frontends/next-dashboard && npm run dev`
2. Open http://localhost:3000
3. DevTools console: ~13 CSP inline-script blocks + eval block
4. Status bar shows "Disconnected", send button disabled even with textarea text

OUT OF SCOPE: McpUiFrame / origin allowlist / validator React components themselves are not reachable for verification because React never hydrates.

Evidence screenshots:
- .agents/.issues/phx2m-r2-csp-breaks-react-refresh-2026-05-29T22-29-00-233Z.png
- .agents/.issues/phx2m-r2-A-blocked-disconnected-2026-05-29T22-30-03-327Z.png

description: In components/agent/src/factory/agent/registry/factories.py, _LazyRegistry inherits from dict and fills with {k: None for k in _FACTORY_KEYS}. __getitem__, get, __iter__, and keys are overridden to lazy-resolve through get_factory(), but items() and values() are NOT — they fall through to the base dict and return None values. No current caller uses .items()/.values() (grep clean), so this is not a live bug, but it's a latent foot-gun: future code iterating items() to dispatch by callable would silently get None. Either override both, or refactor to a thin Mapping wrapper that doesn't expose dict storage. Discovered during bd-s5ev qa verify (memory 086f7d02 chain). Severity: low — no live consumers.
title: QA: _LazyRegistry.items()/.values() leak None instead of resolving factories

acceptance_criteria: Design and land a typed domain-negative result for unknown-backend selection (e.g. a shared helper each get_runner/get_tracker/get_graph/etc factory calls, returning a typed unknown_backend failure with available_backends data instead of raising bare ValueError) across at minimum evals, machine_learning, graph, games, worker, api runtimes. description:
Repo-wide gap in the Polymorphic/Agnostic adapter pattern (runtime/ports.py Protocol + runtime/runtime.py string-keyed dispatch), NOT a violation of the MCP-First tenet -- confirmed against .agents/steering/dev-principles.md: MCP-First governs cross-brick/agent-to-brick calls only, runtime/ internal adapter selection via plain Python is the documented, correct pattern. This bead is about hardening THAT pattern's failure mode, which is currently undocumented/unspecified.

Confirmed instances of the same shape: EvalsRuntime.get_runner (components/evals/src/factory/evals/runtime/runtime.py), TrackingRuntime._create_tracker/get_finetuner/get_timeseries_trainer (components/machine_learning/src/factory/machine_learning/runtime/runtime.py), GraphRuntime._create_graph (components/graph/src/factory/graph/runtime/runtime.py), GamesRuntime (components/games/src/factory/games/runtime/runtime.py), WorkerRuntime (bases/worker/src/factory/worker/runtime/runtime.py), APIRuntime (bases/api/src/factory/api/runtime/runtime.py).

Problem 1 -- lost diagnostic on unknown backend: every one of these factories raises a bare ValueError(f"Unknown {kind} backend: {backend}. Available: {self.available_backends()}") on an unrecognized backend string. The blanket exception-to-ToolResult wrapper in components/mcp_utils/src/factory/mcp_utils/runtime/typed_boundary.py (apply_category, ~line 131-189) catches this before it crosses the MCP wire (so the typed-egress guarantee holds -- no raw exception leaks), but it replaces the specific, actionable message with the generic tool_execution_failed sentinel, indistinguishable from any other internal bug. available_backends() already exists on every one of these runtimes for self-description (used in describe_config_schema/get_capabilities tools) but is never consulted defensively before dispatch to produce a typed domain-negative result (e.g. error=unknown_backend plus available_backends data).

Problem 2 -- no Protocol conformance check at registration: nothing in any of these factories isinstance-checks a concrete adapter against its runtime/ports.py Protocol at construction/registration time. Where @runtime_checkable is used (e.g. learning/runtime/ports.py::RewardSourcePort) it only verifies method NAMES exist, not signatures or completeness. A partially-implemented adapter can be registered and only fail the first time something calls the specific missing method, discovered at call time as an AttributeError swallowed by the same generic tool_execution_failed sentinel.

Discovered while investigating GH issue #746 (FastMCP removal) and a follow-up conversation about whether the RL learning loop's evals_score_gt/evals_evaluate_multi calls were at risk from adapter swaps -- they are NOT (those two tools bypass get_runner entirely, confirmed by direct code read), but the investigation surfaced this real, separate, repo-wide gap in the adapter-dispatch pattern itself.
notes:
META-ARCHITECT VERDICT: APPROVE_WITH_FOLLOWUPS. Split into 3 pieces, not one PR:

1. TIER-1 (mcp_utils only, no migration): the original 'typed unknown-backend failure ToolResult carrying available/requested data' proposal is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE -- ToolResult's own model_validator forbids data on a failed (ok=False) envelope. Real fix: tool_execution_failure() currently logs ONLY the tool identity, discarding the actual exception detail even server-side. Add a SafeDiagnostic(ValueError) marker exception in mcp_utils; factories raise it instead of bare ValueError for expected domain-negative conditions (unknown backend, etc); tool_execution_failure() logs the message ONLY when the exception is a SafeDiagnostic instance (allowlist, not blanket str(exc)) to avoid regressing the existing protected_projection.py::safe_exception precedent (type-identity-only logging to prevent secret/token capture in exception text). Zero DTO/output-contract changes.

2. PROTOCOL CONFORMANCE: add @runtime_checkable to the 7 ports currently missing it (EvalRunner, KnowledgeGraph, GameRules, GameStore, ExperimentTracker, FineTuningPort, TimeSeriesTrainingPort), then a shared mcp_utils validate_adapter(adapter, port) helper called at construction inside each factory. PROVE IN ONE BRICK FIRST (graph -- highest exposure, ~15 tools with unvalidated user-reachable backend param) before rolling to the other five. Graph gotcha: neo4j intentionally implements a narrower contract than full KnowledgeGraph Protocol (excluded from provenance_backends()) -- conformance check must special-case this.

3. PER-BRICK DTO MIGRATION for actual 'tell the caller what backends are valid' recovery (domain-negative successful envelope carrying available/requested per mcp-tools.md's rule) -- this is N separate beads/PRs, one per brick, each a public output-contract migration. NOT implemented in this pass -- deferred, to be filed as follow-up beads per brick when picked up.

This pass implements pieces 1 and 2 (graph-only proof) only.
IMPLEMENTED (this pass): Tier 1 + Tier 2 proof-of-concept, per meta-architect verdict.

Tier 1 (mcp_utils, all 6 bricks benefit immediately, zero migration): added SafeDiagnostic(ValueError) marker exception to components/mcp_utils/src/factory/mcp_utils/runtime/tool_failure.py. tool_execution_failure() now logs the SafeDiagnostic message verbatim (via sys.exc_info()) while staying type-identity-only for any other exception (preserves the existing secret-safe precedent in protected_projection.py::safe_exception). Wire contract unchanged -- still returns the generic tool_execution_failed ToolResult; only the SERVER-SIDE log gains the specific diagnostic.

Tier 2 (graph brick ONLY -- proof-of-concept before repo-wide rollout, per verdict):
- graph/runtime/runtime.py::_create_graph raises SafeDiagnostic instead of bare ValueError on unknown backend.
- Added @runtime_checkable to graph/runtime/ports.py::KnowledgeGraph and graph/runtime/provenance_ports.py::GraphProvenancePort (neither had it before -- confirmed via context-gatherer this was a real prerequisite gap).
- Added module-level protocol-conformance assertions to all 3 concrete adapters (networkx_adapter.py: isinstance since __init__ is side-effect-free; neo4j_adapter.py + persistent_networkx.py: issubclass since __init__ has real driver/blob-storage side effects). Neo4jGraph legitimately passes despite its narrower provenance contract -- documented in KnowledgeGraph/GraphProvenancePort docstrings why (implement + reject-at-call-time via Neo4jProvenanceUnsupportedMixin is the repo's existing idiom, not a Protocol violation).

Verified: uv run pytest components/graph/test components/mcp_utils/test -q -> 463 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (python-factory-7z6o4, confirmed via git stash). foreman_guardian_check clean (new_violations: [], total_violations back to 71 baseline, all touched files at or under 200 LOC).

NOT done this pass (deferred, per verdict's 3-piece split):
- Rollout of Tier 2 (@runtime_checkable + conformance asserts) to machine_learning/games/worker/api's remaining un-decorated ports (EvalRunner, GameRules, GameStore, ExperimentTracker, FineTuningPort, TimeSeriesTrainingPort).
- Tier 3: per-brick output-DTO migration so callers can actually recover from an unknown-backend condition via a successful domain-negative envelope (mcp-tools.md's rule) -- N separate beads, one per brick, each a public output-contract migration. Not started.
title: Adapter-dispatch factories leak generic tool_execution_failed on unknown backend; no Protocol conformance check at registration

description: Every page takes ~3s because each makes 2-5 MCP round-trips through browser>Next.js>Cognito>AgentCore Gateway>Runtime>DynamoDB. Even cached, each hop is ~500-800ms. (2) WATERFALL - App detail fetches app first, THEN fires 3 more calls sequentially. (3) NO CLIENT CACHE - navigating between pages re-fetches everything. Solutions: SWR/TanStack Query for cross-page caching, dedup identical calls, parallelize waterfalls, AbortController with 5s timeout, server-side cache in /api/mcp (60s TTL), MCP-side pagination. close_reason: Fixed locally: set python.terminal.activateEnvironment=false in Kiro user settings. execute_bash confirmed working live (real stdout + accurate exit codes, no reload). Root cause: Python venv auto-activation consumed the first shell-integration completion event; execute_bash closed the terminal before the delayed real event arrived. meshclaw not causal (left only broken agent specs in ~/.kiro/agents). Upstream Kiro bug worth reporting separately.
description: execute_bash tool intermittently/persistently fails silently: returns empty stdout + fabricated Exit Code: 0 without actually running the command (confirmed via independent file-write + read_file checks, and via 'false; echo $?' not returning 1). control_bash_process (background terminal) works reliably as a workaround every time. Ruled out: meshclaw residue (no live process, no LaunchAgent/Daemon, no shell rc references - only inert cache/KB files found), Kiro.app code signature (valid, correct TeamIdentifier), zsh/.zshrc/.zprofile config (correct kiro shell-integration line present and properly placed), DYLD/LD_PRELOAD env vars (none set). Tried: Kiro: Enable Shell Integration setting (already on), Reload Window (did not fix - confirmed still broken post-reload via same file-write test). Matches a known open Kiro bug per internal troubleshooting doc (docs.hub.amazon.dev/docs/kiro/user-guide/troubleshooting) and a live Sage thread (sage.amazon.dev/posts/2018025) with an unresolved comment dated 2026-07-03 ('the issue is still there'). Root cause per internal wiki 1-pager on EC2 shell integration: window reload does not re-invoke shell-env resolution once VSCODE_CLI is set in env, so OSC completion markers between ACP client and terminal never re-sync. Next step to try: full quit (Cmd+Q) and relaunch (not reload). If that fails too, escalate to Kiro team as this looks like an ACP-client-side terminal completion-tracking bug, not a workspace/shell misconfiguration.
title: execute_bash no-ops with fake Exit Code 0 after ACP client switch (meshclaw->kiro)

description:
## Symptom

Companion-X chat agent (Strands-powered) reports it cannot see Veritas query tools. Direct user complaint:

> "The Veritas brick capabilities are surfaced through veritas_get_capabilities, veritas_health_check, and veritas_describe_config_schema only."

User has fresh Midway creds. `call_brick_tool(brick_name="veritas", tool_name="query_veritas", ...)` works fine via the progressive aggregator (returns data, healthy=true, backend=midway). The bug is purely in the chat agent's tool-visibility layer.

## Root cause (confirmed by strands-expert + meta-architect)

Veritas registers 9 of its 12 tools with **bare function names** (no `veritas_` prefix), violating the documented brick-prefix convention:

- BARE: `query_veritas`, `search_resources`, `get_app_topology`, `get_resource_permissions`, `get_security_posture`, `get_deployment_chain`, `get_data_flows`, `list_graph_schema`, `get_app_security_profile`
- PREFIXED (compliant): `veritas_get_capabilities`, `veritas_health_check`, `veritas_describe_config_schema`

The flat-view mount at `/mcp` (`bases/mcp_server/src/factory/mcp_server/runtime/flat_view.py::build_flat_view`) does NOT add a brick prefix on mount — it only renames dot-style to underscore. So the wire-visible names are the bare function names.

Both Companion-X chat paths filter MCP tools by brick prefix. Same root cause manifests through two mechanisms:

**Path 1 — default `StrandsChatAgent`** (when STRANDS_AVAILABLE):
1. `mcp/chat_tool_builder.py::build_chat_tools()` calls `runtime/companion/tools.py::select_tools()`.
2. `select_tools` is fed by `_resolve_available_tools` → `agg.get_all_tool_names()` → `lazy_loader.get_brick_tool_names()`, which **auto-pads bare names with the brick prefix at listing time** (lazy_loader.py: `[n if startswith(pu)/(pd) else f"{pu}{n}" ...]`).
3. So `select_tools` sees `veritas_query_veritas`, `veritas_search_resources`, etc. and includes them in the allowlist.
4. The allowlist is passed to `runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_graph.py::create_mcp_client(allowlist={"veritas_query_veritas", ...})`.
5. `_tool_predicate` then compares `tool.tool_name` (the **wire** name `query_veritas`, unpadded) against the padded allowlist entry `veritas_query_veritas` — **rejected**. The 3 contract tools survive because they're already prefixed at registration.

**Path 2 — `StrandsMCPChatAgent`** (when CHAT_ADAPTER=strands_mcp):
1. Native Strands `MCPClient` over Streamable HTTP to `localhost:{FACTORY_API_PORT}/mcp`.
2. `_tool_filter` regex `^(...|veritas|...)[_.]` is applied directly to `tool.tool_name` (wire name, unpadded).
3. `query_veritas` does not match `^veritas[_.]` — **rejected** outright.

Net effect: in both paths the chat agent only sees the 3 prefixed contract tools, and tells the user the query tools don't exist.

## Why path 1's auto-pad hides this from listing-layer consumers

`get_brick_tool_names` and `get_all_tool_names` always return padded names. So:
- HTTP `/tools` listings, AG-UI route, view discovery, swarm tool allowlist resolution — all see the "fixed" names and look fine.
- The bug is invisible until you cross the **mount** boundary into the actual MCP wire.

This is why the bug has hidden — anything that lists tools is happy. Only when an LLM tries to invoke a tool does the wire-name vs allowlist mismatch surface.

## Files involved

**Veritas (where to fix):**
- `components/veritas/src/factory/veritas/mcp/tools.py` — rename the 9 `@mcp.tool()` registrations to `veritas_query`, `veritas_search_resources`, `veritas_get_app_topology`, `veritas_get_resource_permissions`, `veritas_get_security_posture`, `veritas_get_deployment_chain`, `veritas_get_data_flows`, `veritas_list_graph_schema`, `veritas_get_app_security_profile`. File is ~135 LOC; rename keeps it under 200.

**Internal callers that reference bare names** (must update in lockstep — Polylith monorepo, no external consumers):
- `components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/swarm_tools.py::SWARM_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` — lists `query_veritas`, `search_resources`, `get_app_topology`, `get_app_security_profile`, `get_security_posture`.
- `components/agent/src/factory/agent/registry/redteam_playbooks.py` — references `get_app_security_profile`, `get_resource_permissions`, `get_security_posture` in agent prompts.
- `components/agent/src/factory/agent/skills/veritas-recon/SKILL.md` — references `search_resources` workflow.
- `components/agent/src/factory/agent/registry/defaults_redteam_swarms.py` — references Veritas queries in swarm prompts.

**Drifted prefix lists (fold into this bead):**
- `components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/companion/tools.py::ALLOWED_BRICK_PREFIXES` — has 20 prefixes including `memory`.
- `components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_chat.py::_ALLOWED_RE` — has 19 prefixes, missing `memory`.

These should share one source of truth. Recommend: `strands_mcp_chat.py` imports `ALLOWED_BRICK_PREFIXES` from `companion/tools.py` and builds the regex from it.

## Fix shape (verdict from architects)

**Approved: rename Veritas tools to follow `{brick}_{tool}` convention.**

- Rejected: filter-by-brick-membership (couples chat to aggregator internals; enshrines divergence).
- Rejected: hand-curated EXTRA_TOOLS allowlist (duct tape; accumulates per-brick technical debt).
- Out of scope: mount-time auto-prefixing in flat_view (broader blast radius across all 38 bricks; spawns linked bead).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The 9 Veritas graph query tools are registered with `veritas_` prefix.
2. All internal callers updated (swarm_tools.py, redteam_playbooks.py, skills/veritas-recon/SKILL.md, defaults_redteam_swarms.py — grep for the 9 old names).
3. Drifted prefix lists deduplicated — single source of truth in `companion/tools.py`, regex in `strands_mcp_chat.py` derived from it.
4. Manual verification: spin up Companion-X chat, ask "query Veritas for all VeritasApp nodes." Agent calls `veritas_query` (or equivalent) successfully, returns Cypher results.
5. `foreman_guardian_check` passes.
6. Existing Veritas tests pass with renamed tools.

## Specialist consults logged in companion-x memory

- strands-expert (id `eeb098c6-9bf5-4ff2-b559-59be3c6d8640`): APPROVE_WITH_NOTES — confirmed both paths broken, no SDK bug, rename is most idiomatic.
- meta-architect (id `0ad0033c-c1d9-4815-9629-3a15a7fbcd06`): APPROVE_WITH_NOTES — convention is a hard tenet, file 3 linked beads (this is the narrow P1).

## Reproduction

1. Start Companion-X local stack (lightweight: chromadb/networkx/SQLite/in-memory).
2. Open chat sidebar at http://localhost:3000.
3. Ask: "query veritas to count Ring 2 apps."
4. Observe: chat agent claims `query_veritas` is not in its toolset and offers SIPP / direct UI as alternatives.
5. Confirm via the Companion-X power: `call_brick_tool(brick_name="veritas", tool_name="query_veritas", arguments='{"cypher_query":"MATCH (a:VeritasApp) RETURN count(a)"}')` works.

## Related work to file as discovered-from

- foreman_guardian_check rule that fails on tools whose names don't start with `{brick}_` or `{brick}.`. Surfaces violations at the source diff.
- Audit security and sandbox bricks for mixed dot/underscore styles. Both currently expose tools in both conventions (e.g. `security.code_review` AND `security_pentest_scan`). Determine canonical style or accept both per project policy.
title: Companion-X chat agent can't see Veritas query tools — bare-name registration violates brick-prefix convention

The legacy path is STILL LIVE in 5+ adapters: strands_registered_graph_spawn, strands_graph_spawn, strands_swarm_spawn, strands_subagent_spawn, strands_subagent_async_spawn, mcp/async_tools.py — each calls schedule_rl_loop/run_rl_loop -> games_process_workflow_rl directly, gated by is_rl_eligible which HARDCODES idor-/sast-/dast-/iam- security skills. description: PROBLEM: Every time ada credentials update writes fresh keys to ~/.aws/credentials, all running processes (API at :8000, companion-x power subprocess, MCP server, dashboard) keep using their old in-memory boto3 Session with the now-stale token. This forces a full restart of every process after each refresh. Documented as a footgun in companion-memory.md and project-overview.md. Bites this developer multiple times per day. ROOT CAUSE: boto3 Session reads ~/.aws/credentials once at construction; subsequent calls use cached token until ExpiredTokenException at request time. SDK does not auto-refresh from file. FIX: Wrap session creation in factory.config (or a new factory.aws_session util) with botocore.credentials.RefreshableCredentials.create_from_metadata. The refresh_using callback re-reads ~/.aws/credentials for the configured AWS_PROFILE and returns dict(access_key, secret_key, token, expiry_time). botocore checks expiry on every request and silently refreshes from disk when within the threshold. SCOPE: ~50-80 LOC. Affects every brick that creates boto3 clients (auth, cache, events, graph, kb, llm_gateway, logger, machine_learning, memory, notification, payments, permissions, sandbox, security, storage, telemetry, worker, workflow). The clean implementation is to add factory.config.aws_session_factory() that all AWS adapters call instead of boto3.Session() / boto3.client() directly. Existing AWS adapters at runtime/adapters/aws.py would be migrated. AFFECTED: 13 AWS adapters. ACCEPTANCE: refresh creds with ada, observe API at :8000 picks up new tokens on next Bedrock call without restart; STS GetCallerIdentity from a long-running process succeeds after refresh.
title: Add RefreshableCredentials to boto3 sessions to survive ada credentials update without process restart

description: The Companion-X backend mounts the FastMCP Streamable-HTTP app at /mcp/ as an ASGI sub-app that BYPASSES the parent FastAPI CORSMiddleware. Evidence (backend up on :8000): OPTIONS /ag-ui/run -> 204 with access-control-allow-origin:* / allow-methods POST,OPTIONS / allow-headers Content-Type (chat works cross-origin from the Theia IDE at :3456). OPTIONS /mcp/ -> 405 Method Not Allowed, allow: DELETE,POST, and NO access-control-* headers; POST /mcp/ initialize returns a valid 200 handshake via curl but carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so a browser blocks it. Fix is backend-side: apply CORS (allow origin http://localhost:3456 + the configured dashboard origin, methods POST/DELETE/OPTIONS, headers content-type + mcp-session-id + mcp-protocol-version, expose mcp-session-id) to the mounted MCP ASGI app — NOT only the parent app. Likely in bases/api or projects/companion_x/main.py composition root / mcp_server base mount. Base transport change -> meta-architect gate. Discovered while fixing Theia panel open+render bugs (epic python-factory-ons71).

  g.add_entity(Entity(id='f1',type='Finding',properties={'run_id':'r1'}))

description:
Kiro session (2026-07-23). `TimeGANAdapter`
(`components/machine_learning/src/factory/machine_learning/runtime/adapters/timegan.py`)
is unsupervised: it trains G/D on unlabeled NORMAL signal windows
only, `y_uri` is ignored. It structurally cannot generate failures no
matter how much it's tuned -- there is no failure-mode-conditioned
generator anywhere in the codebase. The 2026-07-21 GAN-loop
experiments (`.github/spec/can-gan-loop-report.md`) show unstable
AUROC across seeds (0.43-0.86), consistent with a GAN that is both
solving the wrong problem and data-starved on ~48MB of real captures.

Current published research (2025-2026) on few-shot fault time-series
generation has moved to diffusion models conditioned on normal-data
pretraining for exactly this low-data regime -- see FaultDiffusion
(arXiv 2511.15174) and Diff-MTS (arXiv 2407.11501), both reporting
diffusion beating GAN baselines on fault synthesis with scarce fault
data.

Do not keep iterating on the current unsupervised TimeGAN loop
expecting it to produce better failures -- it cannot, by construction.
Pick one explicitly:

1. [Recommended near-term, cheapest] Park TimeGAN as documented/tested
   code, invest instead in rule-based correlated injection (see
   companion bead `python-factory-bzm3s`) and real-label validation
   (`sbhyq.1`). Revisit generative modeling only if rule-based
   injection provably still looks "too fake."
2. Build a failure-mode-conditioned generator (conditional GAN or
   few-shot diffusion per the papers above) that takes a
   `failure_mode` label as input, so generator/discriminator
   convergence actually targets failure realism. This is new work, not
   a wiring fix.
3. Do nothing further with GAN loop iterations -- stop burning cycles
   on iteration 9-10 of the current demo-chart plan in the steering
   doc's "Session Resume" section, since the underlying metric
   instability is structural, not a seed-tuning problem.
notes: Closed by upstream commits 0e7e3245 (conditional TimeGAN) + d0574406 (dual-objective loss fix) + a80e7b68/931cddfe (SCANIA pattern extraction). Option 2 from this bead's decision list was picked: a failure-mode-conditioned generator (ConditionalTimeGANAdapter, one-hot failure_mode side channel on both G and D) was built, plus the exact dual-objective loss fix (adversarial-weight taper + diversity loss + one-sided label smoothing) that addresses this bead's diagnosis of *why* the unconditional TimeGAN was unstable. See timegan_conditional.py, timegan_conditional_models.py, timegan_loss.py. New follow-up tracked separately: python-factory (new bead, see can-failure-prediction-review.md addendum 2026-07-24) on the SCANIA-truck-feature-to-CAN-signal-space construct-validity gap this introduces.
title: Decide fate of failure-conditioned generator (park TimeGAN-as-is vs build cGAN/diffusion)

description:
GROUND TRUTH (verified at HEAD, commit 018a8f10, 2026-07-28):

1. Handover doc's claimed root cause is WRONG: _AVG_WINDOW=35 does not
   exist anywhere in git history (checked all commits + all local/remote
   branches). The actual constant is `_AVG_WINDOW = 4` in
   components/dataset/src/factory/dataset/runtime/adapters/failure_injection.py:66,
   unchanged since it was introduced in 58ae5738 (2026-07-15).

2. REAL bug #1 (dead code): `n_events = max(1, target_marked // _AVG_WINDOW)`
   followed by `if target_marked > 0 and n_events == 0: n_events = 1` --
   the second branch is unreachable dead code because max(1, ...) already
   guarantees n_events >= 1 even when target_marked == 0 (i.e. failure_rate
   configured but rounds to 0 events wanted). This forces at least ONE
   3-5-record failure window on every group, no matter how large.

3. REAL bug #2 (structural amplification): can_synthesize dispatches
   inject_failures() PER ARBITRATION ID (see _can_synthesize_dispatch.py),
   not once over the full record stream. Real CAN logs have dozens of
   arbitration IDs, many with small per-ID record counts after multiplier
   expansion (e.g. n_synth=4-20). For small n_synth, floor-division rate
   control (n_events = target_marked // 4) collapses to 1 forced event,
   and 1 event over a 4-20 record group is a 5-100% per-group rate. The
   overall corpus-level rate is the mean of these per-group rates, which
   skews high whenever many CAN IDs have small groups -- reproduced
   ACTUAL_RATE=0.91 vs configured 0.10 with a 100-ID / 1-frame-per-ID /
   multiplier=4 synthetic repro (see below). This structural mismatch
   between "rate control unit = per CAN ID" and "target rate = corpus-wide"
   is the real explanation for the ~89% observed in the handover doc,
   not a miscalibrated window constant.

4. TEST COVERAGE GAP CONFIRMED: none of the 4 commits since the handover
   doc (d49b80c0 correlation, 6d314ecc hybrid, 931cddfe scania extractor,
   0e7e3245 timegan conditional) added a test that asserts actual-vs-
   configured failure rate at the corpus/pipeline level. Ran all 4 test
   files: 83 passed, 2 skipped (external SCANIA fixture, unrelated).
   Every passing assertion is structural ("some failures exist", "labels
   use documented vocabulary", "mode X mutates the right field") -- none
   would fail under the 91% bug.
   - test_correlation_injection.py: only checks failures exist + correct
     mode label, never bounds the rate.
   - test_failure_injection_hybrid.py: bounds the RULE-VS-LEARNED MIX
     ratio (30/70 split, 0.10-0.55 tolerance) but never the overall
     is_failure rate vs failure_rate config.
   - test_scania_pattern_extractor.py / test_timegan_conditional.py:
     don't touch inject_failures/rate control at all (pattern extraction
     and conditional generation, orthogonal path).
   - The ONLY test with rate-adjacent bounds is
     test_can_synthesize.py::test_failure_rate_controls_fraction_of_failures,
     which asserts `fail_high <= 0.8 * len(high)` for failure_rate=0.30 --
     i.e. it explicitly TOLERATES up to 80% observed rate for a 30%
     target, so it would NOT catch the 89%-for-10%-target bug even if it
     ran. It's SKIPPED anyway (requires MF4 fixture at hardcoded
     /Users/danielrodrigo/Downloads/CAN Data, absent on this machine).
   - test_can_e2e_qa.py has `assert failure_rate_actual <= 0.5` for a
     0.1 target -- also too loose, and also skipped (same missing
     fixture).
   - The only automatic detector in production code is
     verify_failure_rate() in _post_injection_verification.py, which
     only logs a WARNING (never raises, never returns a signal) when
     |actual - expected| > 0.05. No test asserts on this log output
     (no caplog usage found for this module) -- confirmed via grep.

5. MINIMUM TEST THAT WOULD CATCH IT: a corpus-level (not single-group)
   property test that (a) calls the can_synthesize dispatch path (or
   inject_failures directly) across MULTIPLE small groups simulating
   realistic per-CAN-ID record counts, (b) computes actual_rate =
   total_failures / total_records across ALL groups combined, and
   (c) asserts abs(actual_rate - configured_rate) <= some tight tolerance
   (e.g. 0.03-0.05), for both single-group and multi-group/many-small-
   groups scenarios. None of the existing tests operate at this
   multi-group corpus level; they all check a single inject_failures()
   call on one homogeneous record list, which hides the amplification
   effect of many small per-ID groups.

Also found (separate, pre-existing) test breakage unrelated to the rate
bug: test_can_failure_modes.py::test_ecu_timeout_zeros_signals and
::test_signal_freeze_holds_constant FAIL at HEAD because
_physical_failure_modes.py (landed in 018a8f10, replacing the legacy
_rule_failure_helpers dispatch) no longer zeros signals / freezes to
exact constant values the way the old _RULE_DISPATCH did -- the tests
were written against the pre-physical-modes semantics and never updated.
Filed as evidence of drift but out of scope for the rate bug itself.
title: QA: rate-mismatch bug in failure_injection.py still reproducible; no test asserts actual-vs-target rate

description: The rt-scan-vulns swarm tested IDOR by querying DynamoDB tables directly with AWS CLI. This is wrong for two reasons: (1) In a real AWS service, an attacker doesn't have DynamoDB access — they interact through API Gateway/Lambda endpoints. Direct DB access is an infra misconfiguration, not an app-layer IDOR. (2) The GT finding is 'unauthorized user can delete vet clinics via POST /yourpets/vet/remove' — a REST API endpoint IDOR. The agents never tested through the API layer and never touched the Vets table. Fix requires: (a) rt-app-deploy must create API Gateway endpoints that proxy to Lambda, not just bare Lambda functions. (b) rt-scan-vulns must test through HTTP endpoints (curl against API Gateway), not direct DynamoDB. (c) The Vets table must be included with proper schema and test data. (d) A /yourpets/vet/remove endpoint must exist for the agents to test against.
title: IDOR red team tests DynamoDB directly instead of through API — misses GT finding

description: CWE-346. Affected brick: evals. ClosedReviewRunner copies provider/model/deployment/persona provenance from ReviewerSlot while every slot executes the same NoVerdictReviewer, which ignores those declared identities. Independence compares the copied strings and quorum counts terminal success, so multiple claimed independent reviewers can be one deterministic local function. Remediation: derive and authenticate provenance from the actual reviewer execution/provider receipt and require policy independence over verified execution identities/implementations.
title: Security: Evals reviewer quorum uses configured identities, not executed provenance
