description: The graph brick was designed polymorphic (networkx + neo4j adapters via runtime/ports.py), and exposes typed tools graph_find_entities, graph_get_neighbors, graph_get_dashboard_summary, security.list_persisted_findings, evals_get_dashboard_summary, games_get_dashboard_summary. But Cypher queries leak past the polymorphic boundary in 3 layers, breaking everything when running on networkx (local dev): (Layer 1 UI) frontends/next-dashboard/lib/hooks/use-findings.ts and use-timeline-data.ts call graph_query with raw Cypher strings; (Layer 2 brick adapters) security/runtime/adapters/graph_persistence.py:get_findings, games/runtime/_rl_stages.py, games/runtime/workflow_report_findings.py, games/runtime/workflow_report_graph.py, games/runtime/workflow_report_target.py, events/runtime/dispatch_args.py — all build Cypher strings via graph_graph_query; (Layer 3 skills+prompts) idor-validate/SKILL.md, sast-open-scan/SKILL.md, dast-open-scan/SKILL.md, compx-platform/SKILL.md, veritas-recon/SKILL.md, redteam_service_mocks.py, redteam_eval_addenda.py, redteam_playbooks.py, defaults_code_scan_*.py, defaults_dast_open.py, defaults_sandbox_graph.py — agents are instructed to call graph_query(cypher=MATCH...). Symptoms: empty Findings tab, no RL loop visible, no evals running post-workflow, empty Timeline. Root cause is single: Cypher does not parse on networkx. Fix means tightening the polymorphic boundary so only the graph brick's neo4j adapter ever sees Cypher; everyone else queries through typed brick tools. Future neo4j→DynamoDB or any other backend swap should be one config change.
title: EPIC: Cypher leak — backend-specific queries throughout UI bricks skills

description: In strands_swarm_spawn.py, after the async for loop over swarm.stream_async(task), run_rl_loop() is called SYNCHRONOUSLY. run_rl_loop() calls invoker('games_process_workflow_rl', ...) which resolves to aggregator.invoke_tool() -> lazy_loader.call_brick_tool_sync() -> instrumentation.traced_tool_call_sync() -> pools._run_sync_agent(). _run_sync_agent detects a running event loop and submits the work to _AGENT_POOL via future.result() — a blocking .result() call on the current thread. description: strands-expert review of 2zrj2 (APPROVE_WITH_FOLLOWUPS). Two issues: (1) The max_cycles-derived cap nodes*(cycles+1) is set as an explicit bound that defeats the platform-default floor (25), so it can be TIGHTER than default. Because Strands fan-in nodes re-fire per predecessor completion (no join barrier, graph.py _is_node_ready_with_conditions), a legitimate ACYCLIC DAG can need >nodes executions (e.g. A->B,A->C,B->C = C runs twice), so a future graph with max_cycles=1 could hit should_continue and terminate status=FAILED mid-run. Fix: floor the derived cap at the platform default -> max(nodes*(cycles+1), platform_default), or base headroom on DAG depth/fan-in. REDTEAM itself is immune (linear, 5<<10). (2) No validation guard on max_cycles: 0 -> single-pass truncation; -1 -> derived 0 -> instant FAILED bricks the graph. Add 'if max_cycles is not None and max_cycles < 1: raise ValueError' mirroring the max_node_executions guard in GraphConfig._validate_execution_contract.
title: max_cycles translation can truncate legitimate fan-in DAGs + no guard on max_cycles<1

So vuln_class='IDOR' (uppercase, valid case-insensitive) renders as 'Use the `IDOR-code-scan` skill' which the regex doesn't match, so the validator silently passes even though no IDOR-code-scan/SKILL.md exists (skills dir uses lowercase). Same gap for any unicode/non-ASCII vuln_class. The launcher correctly catches empty/whitespace vuln_class via the missing-required-context-var check, and correctly catches lowercase typos like 'bogusvuln' via the static-backtick regex. The lowercase-canonical convention from bd-2xbi (qa memory 89c8333d) was supposed to be normalized at config-read time; here a similar normalization should happen at the validator boundary (lower() before regex matching) OR launch_validator's _STATIC_BACKTICK regex should be case-insensitive. Reproducer: components/agent/src/factory/agent/registry/launch_validator.py with vuln_class='IDOR' or unicode passes [], but skills/IDOR-code-scan/SKILL.md does not exist.
title: QA: launch_validator does not gate uppercase or unicode vuln_class through workflow factory

description:
PROBLEM: the recursive-learning reward signal is pinned to security "findings". The loop's only reward producer is games_process_workflow_rl -> evals_score_gt (findings vs gt_entries.json) -> reward = F1*100, gated by is_rl_eligible (findings-producing skills or graph_* tools). This is a domain leak (de-facto `if domain == security`) into the ENGINE, violating North Star #2 (domain = data, not branch). Non-finding work — ordinary chat, any non-security domain agent — can never be scored, rewarded, or learned from. Only spawned `swarm.completed`/`graph.completed` runs feed the loop; the main chat turn earns nothing.

GOAL: make reward a domain-agnostic POLYMORPHIC source. A reward signal = {scalar, verdict, provenance}. GT-findings becomes ONE adapter among several emitting the SAME neutral reward.computed contract (already domain-neutral: RewardComputedPayload has score/reward_value/verdict).

FRAMEWORK-FIRST (reuse what exists; no new ML, no bespoke RL):
- User feedback: chat-feedback.ts (bd-2dq6) already captures thumbs up/down to memory but dead-ends — wire it as an explicit reward source.
- LLM-as-judge: evals_evaluate / evals_evaluate_multi already exist (rubric-based, domain-agnostic, unused by the loop).
- Oracle verdict: the domain-agnostic oracle brick verdict (suspected->proven) as reward.
- Telemetry: tool failures/retries/errors from the events bus as negative reward/penalty.
- Findings/GT: demote to one adapter.
- Also: score the MAIN chat turn, not only spawned runs.

UNBLOCKS the offline trajectory landing-zone (every domain now yields scored trajectories).

DESIGN GATE (required before code): meta-architect (reward-source seam + neutral contract + zero domain branch) + strands-expert (how reward/recall attach to the live chat agent via Strands hooks/plugins). Out of scope: real RL algorithm, distillation training job.

acceptance_criteria: Each handshake, commitment, challenge, review slot, and native execution has a 256-bit Evals-issued nonce bound to its domain/context; nonce reuse with a different payload or operation is rejected; exact idempotent replay policy is explicit; old verify-only keys validate historical records after rotation; new writes use only the active key; unknown/revoked/wrong-purpose keys fail; cross-operation, cross-evaluation, preseed, reseal, nonce-replay, and rotation tests pass.
description: CWE-294. Affected brick: evals. Execution attestations bind context and use constant-time HMAC verification, but carry no Evals-issued random nonce and verify_exact resolves challenge/native records against the signer's current active_key_id. Cross-operation/preseed replay policy is therefore incomplete, and a safe key rotation makes valid old records fail even while the old key remains trusted. Remediation: add purpose-bound random operation nonces, trusted nonce-to-payload binding, envelope-key-id verification through a rotation-aware verifier keyring, and signed allowed-key purpose/epoch authority.
title: Security: Evals attestation nonce and key rotation semantics are incomplete

description:
Found during bd-c9gk verify pass.

Symptom
-------
After v1 theme override removal (bd-c9gk), the cpk-web-inspector diamond renders at full 48x48 inside the 24px status bar instead of the intended ~22x22.

Root cause
----------
frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/inspector.css contains:
  .copilot-status-host cpk-web-inspector { transform: scale(0.45); ... }
But the underlying Lit component (CopilotKit v2 dev inspector) sets style="transform: none; ..." inline on its host element. Inline styles win over external stylesheets without the important flag, so scale(0.45) never applies.

Evidence (playwright):
- getBoundingClientRect on cpk-web-inspector -> width=48 height=48
- getComputedStyle(...).transform === 'none'
- matched CSSOM rule still shows scale(0.45) but is overridden by inline style

Reproduction
------------
1. Source projects/companion_x/.env, start API and next-dashboard
2. Open localhost:3000
3. Inspect status bar (bottom right) - diamond is full-size and overflows the 24px slot
4. DevTools: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('cpk-web-inspector')).transform === 'none'

Fix options (smallest first)
----------------------------
A) Add the important flag to inspector.css transform/width/height/margin rules
B) Hoist the scale to the .copilot-status-host wrapper instead of the inner element (transform applied to parent is not affected by child inline style)
C) Wrap cpk-web-inspector in an additional scaling parent so inline transform on the inspector itself does not matter

Severity
--------
Visual polish only - chat, tool cards, thinking panel all work. Diamond is functional, just oversized. p2 polish bug, not a blocker for c9gk.
title: QA c9gk: cpk-web-inspector overflows status bar (Lit inline transform overrides scale rule)

description:
Gap: every failure label in Rando is a hand-coded deterministic mutation (failure_injection.py, 8 modes: signal_drift, drop_to_zero, out_of_sequence, sensor_degradation, ecu_timeout, signal_freeze, spike_noise, correlation_break). No real fault timestamps exist anywhere in the pipeline. Current LightGBM AUROC 0.97-1.00 per CAN ID measures "can the model detect our own injected mutation," which is a materially easier task than "can it predict a real vehicle failure" — some CAN IDs hitting AUROC 1.000 with F1 flagged 0/1 is a signature of a too-easy synthetic task, not evidence of real predictive power.

Field context: synthetic failure injection ("the anomaly assumption") is a real, named weak-supervision technique, but the generalization gap between injected and real failure signatures is an explicitly documented open problem in the literature.

Fix, in priority order:
1. Source or construct a small set of REAL labeled fault episodes (even a labeled subset of a public dataset like Car-Hacking/OTIDS, or any DTC-linked real episode) and validate current LightGBM/LSTM/TCN performance against them. This is the single highest-value experiment — determines whether the construct-validity concern is theoretical or actually biting.
2. Lean into multi-signal correlated injection (correlation_break is the closest existing mode to how real faults usually manifest) over single-signal modes (drop_to_zero, freeze) as the primary training signal; treat single-signal modes as weaker positive controls.
3. In all reporting/dashboards, label current metrics explicitly as "detection of injected synthetic patterns," not "failure prediction accuracy," until step 1 is done.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 4.
title: Validate CAN failure labels against real fault data (synthetic-injection construct-validity gap)

description:
Gap: can_keystone.py's run_keystone_pipeline() (the function behind the can_run_full_pipeline MCP tool) hardcodes a fixed stage list — ingest, profile, synthesize (SDV only, via recipe://local/can-synthesize@1), window, augment, LightGBM — and never calls ml_train_timeseries(model_type="timegan") or ml_sample_timeseries anywhere. TimeGAN itself (timegan.py) is real, unit-tested, adversarially-trained code, correctly implementing generator-vs-discriminator training — but it is dead code with respect to the production pipeline. It's also only trained on unlabeled normal signal windows, not failure modes (y_uri is explicitly ignored for timegan per the MCP tool docstring), so even if wired in it would not currently generate model-driven failure examples (see the companion issue on hand-coded failure injection).

Additionally: current field trajectory (2024-2026 papers) shows diffusion models (TabDDPM, Diffusion-TS, CSDI) overtaking GANs as SOTA for time-series synthesis, and both GAN and diffusion families are documented as data-hungry — likely a poor fit for Rando's ~67 files / 48MB real-data corpus. TimeGAN maturation should be deprioritized relative to the label-validation gap (see companion issue), not invested in further right now.

Decision options (pick one explicitly, don't leave ambiguous):
1. [Recommended near-term] Leave TimeGAN as a documented, tested experiment; do not wire into can_keystone.py. Revisit only after real-label validation (companion issue) is done and if signal-fidelity (not label quality) turns out to be the actual bottleneck.
2. [If pursued] Build a conditional-GAN variant that takes a failure_mode label as generator input, so the adversarial loop can eventually target failure synthesis, not just normal-signal realism. This is the technically correct way to make "GAN vision" (generator improves, discriminator improves, both converge) actually apply to the failure side of the pipeline, which today it does not.
3. [If pursued] Evaluate a lightweight temporal VAE or revisit diffusion-based synthesis, but only once real fault data volume justifies a deep generative model.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md sections 2 and 6.
title: Deprioritize TimeGAN maturation; wire or explicitly park GAN-based failure synthesis

description:
Gap: the spec (Rando.md, ml-dataset-generation.md) states the goal is a "closed-loop adversarial system... graded by evaluation metrics, until models achieve production-quality." No such loop exists in code. can_inference.py's CanInferenceBridge is a complete, working batch-inference class with ZERO connections to games, evals_persist_score, or memory_store anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by grep — it only appears in its own module, lazy-load registry, and MCP wrapper). Nothing feeds live inference errors, false alarms, or newly labeled episodes back into retraining.

Field context: production PHM systems favor drift-triggered retraining (PSI/KS/JS-divergence monitoring, e.g. Evidently AI/whylogs) over calendar-based retraining. Critically, a 2024 finding shows self-generated labels fed back into retraining WITHOUT a confirmation/filtering gate cause silent performance degradation over successive cycles.

Fix, in priority order (the plumbing already exists generically in events/games/memory per the platform's domain-agnostic substrate — this is wiring, not new infrastructure, except item 3):
1. Wire can_inference.py -> memory_store using the episode-tagging convention already specified in Rando.md section 10.5 (tags=["can-episode", ...]). This alone gets most of the way to a feedback loop.
2. Wire can_inference.py outputs into the events brick's learning contracts / rewards plumbing (same pattern games/workflow_rl.py already uses via get_service("tool_invoker")).
3. Design and implement a confirmation gate BEFORE wiring anything into games/RL retraining — decide what "confirmed" means for a real vehicle (DTC log match? human review?) so the system doesn't quietly reinforce its own synthetic-label biases. This is the one genuinely new component needed; do not skip it when wiring 1-2.
4. Add calibration-drift monitoring (not just static training-time Brier score) once live inference exists, plus a cost-sensitive/economic threshold instead of a fixed probability cutoff.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md sections 5 and 7.
title: Wire live inference feedback loop with confirmation gate (memory/events/games)

description:
Gap: the evals brick has 6 real, correctly-implemented, unit-tested CAN computational evaluators (can_auroc, can_auprc, can_brier, can_lead_time, can_false_alarm, can_episode_recall — plus 4 synthetic-data-fidelity evaluators: can_distribution_similarity, can_temporal_coherence, can_statistical_fidelity, can_mode_coverage) registered in evaluator_catalog.py. A bundler function evaluate_can_model() in evals/runtime/adapters/can_evaluator.py already wraps the classifier subset correctly. NONE of this is called by can_keystone.py's training loop — train_top_can_ids() (machine_learning/runtime/can_keystone_helpers.py) computes its own inline sklearn-style metrics via timeseries_metrics.py instead, duplicating logic that already exists correctly in evals.

Meta-architect verdict (already obtained): this is pure wiring debt, not a Polylith/dependency-direction violation. Two compounding gaps, both small:
(a) evaluate_can_model() has no MCP facade — only the lower-level evals_evaluate_computational(evaluator_name, ...) tool exists (scores one metric at a time on raw arrays). Nobody built the one-call convenience wrapper.
(b) machine_learning never calls evals at all — should push results to evals after training (not the other way around), using the exact same idiom the games brick's workflow_rl.py already uses: get_service("tool_invoker") from factory.mcp_utils.interface, then invoker("evals_evals_persist_score", ...) by bare tool-name string, no direct import of factory.evals.

Concrete fix (two additive changes, both small):
1. In evals/mcp/evaluator_tools.py, add a thin @mcp.tool() wrapper `evals_evaluate_can_model(y_true, y_pred, y_score)` that calls the existing evaluate_can_model() function. No new business logic — matches brick-anatomy.md.
2. In machine_learning/runtime/can_keystone_helpers.py::train_top_can_ids, after each trainer.train(...) call, look up the tool invoker and push validation predictions to the new evals tool, following workflow_rl.py's best-effort try/except pattern (log-and-swallow on failure, never raise).

Open design fork needing a decision before implementation: TimeSeriesTrainingJob.metrics is currently a flat dict[str,float] with no raw y_val/y_pred/y_score arrays to forward. Options: (a) widen the training job record to stash validation-split arrays at fit time [cheaper at runtime, touches a shared Pydantic contract], or (b) call trainer.predict(job.id, X_val_uri) after training to regenerate y_pred/y_score via the existing TimeSeriesTrainingPort.predict contract [architecturally cleaner, costs a redundant inference pass]. Route this specific fork through meta-architect + implementer before coding, since it spans two bricks and a shared contract shape.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 5; meta-architect consult transcript in session history.
title: Wire evals CAN evaluator harness into can_keystone training loop

description:
Kiro session (2026-07-24), following up after pulling upstream commits
931cddfe (SCANIA pattern extraction), 0e7e3245 (conditional TimeGAN),
d0574406 (dual-objective loss fix), and 6d314ecc (hybrid injection +
can_synthesize integration). See
.github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 17 for full writeup.

## What shipped (good news first)

1. jln5n (TimeGAN fate) is effectively resolved: ConditionalTimeGANAdapter
   adds a one-hot failure_mode side channel to both G and D
   (timegan_conditional.py, timegan_conditional_models.py) -- this is
   "option 2" from that bead. timegan_loss.py's dual-objective loss
   (adversarial-weight taper as AUROC rises, diversity-loss to fight mode
   collapse, one-sided label smoothing) is a textbook fix for the exact
   instability diagnosed previously (review doc section 16.1).
2. injection_strategy="hybrid" in can_synthesize.py / failure_injection.py
   gives a clean rule/learned/hybrid (30/70) split, and the reported AUROC
   lift (0.50-0.60 simple injection -> 0.70-0.80 SCANIA-pattern injection,
   per can-gan-loop-report.md) is a genuinely interesting result.

## The new gap this introduces

ScaniaPatternExtractor takes SCANIA APS truck data's 170 anonymized
histogram/counter features and builds an invented 50-frame linear
interpolation "drift toward failure" trajectory (SCANIA is tabular
snapshot data, not real time series -- the temporal shape is synthetic).
match_signals() / resample_time() then reshape this to whatever
signal-count/frame-count the actual CAN data needs: extra CAN signals
beyond SCANIA's 170 get padded with Gaussian noise matched to the window's
own std, not real content, and time mismatches use linear interpolation.

This means "SCANIA-derived realism" is: real repair-labeled tabular truck
data -> invented temporal trajectory -> truncated/interpolated/noise-padded
into a shape with no semantic relationship to the target CAN signal names
(RPM, coolant_temp, etc). It's a real improvement over hand-coded
drop-to-zero/freeze (there IS a real distribution underneath now), but it
is not "real CAN failure signatures" and shouldn't be reported as closing
the section 4/9.1 construct-validity gap. The AUROC lift most likely
reflects "SCANIA's real failure statistics are a harder, more realistic
anomaly distribution than hand-coded drop-to-zero" -- a legitimate finding
-- but not evidence the model learned Toyota/Kia coolant-temp dynamics.

## Ask

1. Relabel the 0.70-0.80 AUROC numbers in can-gan-loop-report.md and the
   steering doc as "detects SCANIA-derived anomaly statistics reshaped into
   CAN signal space" not "realistic CAN failures" until (2) is answered.
2. Decide: is noise-padding non-SCANIA-covered CAN signals the intended
   long-term design or a placeholder? Document the decision either way.
3. Fully decoupled from python-factory-bzm3s (rule-based correlated
   injection) -- different complementary axis, not blocked by this.

Reference: .github/spec/can-failure-prediction-review.md section 17.

description:
## Symptom

Companion-X chat sidebar no longer renders the Thinking panel
(`<CopilotChatReasoningMessage>`) on assistant turns. User reports
"we used to show thought as a call inside chat but that's no longer
displayed". Confirmed via Playwright probe of the running API process
and SSE-stream inspection on `/ag-ui/run`: zero `REASONING_MESSAGE_*`
events emitted across a chat run.

## Root cause

Two-edged config gap, not a code bug:

1. `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL` is empty in the running API process env
   (verified via `ps eww`). Falls through to `_resolve_chat_model()`
   returning `None`, then `build_chat_model(None)` -> `_resolve_model(None)`
   picks a Strands default. The default may resolve to a thinking-capable
   model (chat says "I am Claude") but the model_id passed into
   `_supports_thinking()` is None, so the predicate fails.

2. `COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET` is unset. `_thinking_budget()`
   returns 0. With budget=0, `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking`
   is never attached to the BedrockModel - Sonnet does not emit
   `reasoning_text` events, AG-UI mapper has nothing to translate
   into `REASONING_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END`, CopilotKit's Thinking
   panel has nothing to render.

Strands and FE pipeline are both fine. Canary tests pass:
- components/agent/test/factory/agent/test_strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
  pins BedrockModel `_get_additional_request_fields` shape.
- bases/api/test/factory/api/test_ag_ui_chat_reasoning.py pins the
  AG-UI trio when `reasoning_text` events arrive.

## Fix (env-only path, ships immediately)

Set in projects/companion_x/.env:

  COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
  COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET=16000

Restart the API. SSE stream now emits the trio; Thinking panel renders.

## Bigger fix (UX-correct path) — file as discovered-from sub-issue

User feedback: "that env variable should ALWAYS be on" and "I always
assume all models think". Three follow-ups make the experience match
the mental model:

1. Flip `_thinking_budget()` default from 0 to a sane budget (e.g. 8192)
   when env unset. Treat empty/"0" as explicit-off only. Cost note:
   Bedrock bills thinking output separately at the per-token rate, so
   default-on is a real cost decision — needs strands-expert consult on
   the budget number before flipping.

2. Default `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL` to a thinking-capable model
   (Sonnet 4.6) in .env.example and the local-dev README so a fresh
   clone gets thinking out of the box.

3. Optional: small UI hint in chat header when active model is not
   thinking-capable so user understands why the panel is silent.
   (Haiku/Nova/Llama/GLM5/GPT-OSS cannot natively emit reasoning.)

## Repro

1. Start API with `COMPANION_X_CHAT_MODEL=` (empty) and
   `COMPANION_X_CHAT_THINKING_BUDGET` unset.
2. Open dashboard, send any chat message.
3. Inspect DevTools Network -> POST /ag-ui/run SSE stream. Filter
   for "REASONING_MESSAGE_". Result: zero matches.
4. <CopilotChatReasoningMessage> slot never mounts. Thinking panel
   never appears.

## Acceptance

- Env vars set; SSE stream contains REASONING_MESSAGE_START +
  >=1 REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT + REASONING_MESSAGE_END per chat turn.
- Thinking panel renders inline above the assistant message.
- Both pinned tests still pass:
    pytest components/agent/test/factory/agent/test_strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
    pytest bases/api/test/factory/api/test_ag_ui_chat_reasoning.py

## Files involved (read-only context)

- projects/companion_x/.env (config gap)
- projects/companion_x/.env.example (default-on fix candidate)
- components/agent/src/factory/agent/runtime/adapters/strands_mcp_chat_thinking.py
  (_thinking_budget, _supports_thinking, build_chat_model)
- components/ui/src/factory/ui/runtime/ag_ui_mapper_chat.py
  (_on_reasoning_text, _close_reasoning_if_open)
- frontends/next-dashboard/lib/copilotkit/reasoning-slot.tsx
- frontends/next-dashboard/components/chat/copilot-sidebar.tsx
  (messageView.reasoningMessage slot)

## Tenet

dev-principles.md — Companion-X local dev should "just work" without
env-var-fu. SDK-First: Strands provides the primitive, our defaults
should make it visible by default in dev.

description: Strands Swarm shares state across nodes via SharedContext.context: dict[node_id, dict[str, Any]] (verified at strands/multiagent/swarm.py:121 and Swarm._build_node_input swarm.py:609). Each handoff appends to it; the dict is rebuilt verbatim into every subsequent agent's synthetic input prompt. Long swarm runs (10+ handoffs with rich context payloads) bloat that synthetic prompt monotonically. NO BUILT-IN PRIMITIVE in Strands 1.35 to bound this. Fix: author components/agent/src/factory/agent/plugins/swarm_shared_context_pruner.py — a HookProvider that listens on BeforeNodeCallEvent and prunes/summarizes swarm.shared_context.context to last N entries (or by total token estimate) before each agent runs. ~80 LOC. Configurable: max_entries=10 default, prune strategy (FIFO, LRU, summarize-then-keep). Distinct from ContextOffloader (which fixes tool-result bloat per agent — different problem, see python-factory-<TBD-context-offloader>). Discovered in strands-expert wave4-candidates audit. Defer until production swarm runs actually surface the issue — this is preemptive engineering.

description:
Owner idea captured 2026-08-05. NOT being built yet.

Full write-up, including the counterarguments: projects/loaf_pattern_intel/docs/ai-functions-hypothesis.md

Owner framing: code that calls Bedrock for EXECUTION rather than code that runs then calls Bedrock for inspection. An AI function is a typed callable whose implementation is a model call. Not a factory primitive yet. Strands structured output is the building block; what is missing is the function abstraction plus model pinning plus a binding to the eval harness.

Four positions on the rule to AI-function spectrum:

1. AI aids rule authoring and mutation. Already the plan for milestone one. Shipped artifact stays a plain deterministic rule, so no new governance problem.

2. AI as the PRECISION STAGE behind a deliberately noisy high-recall rule that fires but reports low confidence. STRONGEST of the four. It makes the 7 percent FP bar a property of the pipeline rather than of the rule alone, which unlocks rule families currently rejected as too noisy. It is measurable, because combined precision scores on the same versioned cases. And it is a real candidate to automate the owning team requirement that a second SAST engineer triages results independently. Cost is bounded by hit count, not corpus size.

3. AI function REPLACES the scanner rule. This is where the chaos the owner worried about actually lives. It breaks corpus-scale economics, reproducibility, and diffability, and an AI function is not an ACAT shim so it has nowhere to run inside DiRT today. Deepest issue is reproducibility: versioned evaluation assumes same inputs give same outputs.

4. AI eval replaces DiRT-rule-passing as the bar. Riskiest. If the same model family grades both the candidate and its own output, the loop can agree with itself while escape rate does not move. Needs a held-out human-labelled set, and only 71 of 774 AppStar-led escapes have any human response, so that set is small and self-selected.

Why this matters beyond novelty: the F, R, and V buckets mean roughly a quarter of the 88 verdict-log rows are NOT expressible as a static rule at all. R rows need enforced defaults plus review-time context such as authenticated principal, object ownership, or data classification. V rows need someone to inspect the real call path. So DiRT-rule-passing has a known ceiling, and an AI function is a candidate instrument for exactly that gap.
title: PARKED: AI functions as prevention controls - aid, augment, or replace scanner rules

description:
Supersedes the invented shape in ts5ox.5. Mirror the real Smithy model from DiscoveryRuleTestingLambdaModel.

InitiateJob request: jobId is REQUIRED and client-minted, plus profileObj, packageFilters with packageListFilter / languageMapFilter / statusFilter / maxCount, isHeavyJob, and timeout config. Response contains ONLY jobStatus, statusMessage, timestamps, createdBy - NO jobId.

GetJob returns Job with jobId, status, statusMessage, jobTitle, jobMessage, actor, packageCount, metrics, errors.

ListScans filtered to status FAILED gives the failures stream. Its errors map is keyed by the nine Failures constants: ScanPublishingFailure, PackageSnapshotResolutionError, PackageNotFound, SnapshotAccessError, ScanCreationFailure, ScanArtifactSourcingFailure, ShimRunningFailure, ResultPublishingFailure, ArtifactUploadFailure.

ListFindings returns Finding with jobId, findingId, findingMetadata as an opaque JSON string, findingLocations each with startPath / endPath / message where the line number is inline as hash L10, plus packageName, branchName, commitId, ownership, analyzerName, ruleName. There is NO severity field and NO integer line field.

All three list operations are paginated on nextToken.

Statuses, exactly six, three terminal: SUBMITTED, IN_PROGRESS, FINALIZING, COMPLETE, FAILED, CANCELLED. It is COMPLETE not COMPLETED. TIMED_OUT does not exist.

Model the rollback path: if the post-create notification fails the service deletes the job and demands a NEW id, so a submit can fail leaving no job record at all. That is what submission_attempt in the contract records.

Model the recovery path: ListJobs filtered by actor, status, and a recent-days window. There is no query-by-rule.

Branch pinning: use the JSONL package list path. Each line is a JSON array of packageName plus branchName entries, branchName mandatory and non-blank. This bypasses SigmaDelta and honours the branch named. The default CSV path resolves through a snapshot store keyed on package name alone and gives one arbitrary branch per package.

Keep scan scope a closed enum. Keep the deterministic jobId derived from rule candidate revision, scan scope, and submission attempt.
title: loaf-intel: rebuild dirt_mock against the VERIFIED DiRT contract

acceptance_criteria: Custom evaluators registered through the evals brick produce an immutable run record per case. A candidate that misses a rubric criterion is scored as missing THAT criterion by name. FP-rate scoring states its sample size and confidence level. A scan that did not pin branches is flagged, and its null findings are never scored as evidence of absence.
description:
Use the evals brick with CUSTOM evaluators, not the 20-plus strands-agents-evals built-ins. The built-ins grade generic LLM behaviour such as helpfulness and faithfulness. What this project grades is whether a rule candidate is DEFENSIBLE, which is a domain judgement against the verdict-log rubric and DiRT's own quality bar.

Score these:

1. The five verdict-log rubric criteria, per criterion, naming the evidence that satisfied or missed each one.

2. FP rate against the OWNING TEAM bar, not the agent skill heuristic. The owning team wiki, owner appsec-ace, states a goal of 7 percent or lower FP rate, sampling at 90 percent confidence with a 5 percent margin of error, and independent triage by a second SAST engineer. The Dirtyy skill 50 percent failure-rate gate is agent-authored - keep it as a secondary signal, but it is not the bar.

3. Scan-failure rate and ShimRunningFailure clustering.

4. Whether the scan pinned branches. An unpinned null result is NOT evidence of absence, because the default path scans one arbitrary branch per package. Never score it as such.

One built-in IS worth using: a tool-trajectory evaluator to confirm the agent actually called get_escape_evidence before proposing an invariant, rather than inventing one.

Cases are versioned and seeded from the verdict log.
title: loaf-intel: custom evals evaluators encoding the owning-team quality bar

description: spawn-hooks.tsx useSpawnSubagentRenderer calls <SubAgentToolRows /> without passing the spawnToolCallId prop. The SubAgentToolRows component has a primary O(1) lookup path that uses spawnToolCallId to find nested sub-agent tool calls via parentMessageId. Without this prop, it always falls back to the positional scan (walk backward through messages to find last spawn_* anchor). The positional scan is fragile and breaks when multiple spawns happen in a turn, or when sub-agent tool calls arrive in a different message batch than the spawn anchor. The fix requires: (1) the useRenderTool render callback must expose the tool's callId, OR (2) the spawned card must read it from agent.messages. Checking CopilotKit useRenderTool signature: the render function receives {name, status, parameters, result} — toolCallId is NOT exposed in the public API. This means spawnToolCallId can only be obtained by scanning agent.messages inside the render function to find the toolCallId matching this spawn. This is the same positional scan SubAgentToolRows does anyway. Root cause: CopilotKit useRenderTool does not expose toolCallId to render callbacks. The wipnv parentMessageId nesting work is complete on the backend but the frontend primary path is unreachable.
title: QA: spawnToolCallId never passed to SubAgentToolRows — primary parentMessageId nesting path dead

description:
Security-engineer finding (F4 HIGH + F5 MED) from the MessagingPort SME consult (GH #798). PRE-EXISTING gap in the merged egress rail: ProviderRoute.required_scopes is documented as 'the only source of scope authority' but is NEVER enforced anywhere, and HttpRefreshTokenAcquirer requests the provider.scopes UNION ignoring the route. Today impact is low (one route per connection), but it blocks the 'one credential, many capabilities' model and is latent over-privilege (CWE-862/863).

FIX:
1. Persist the granted scopes at enrollment (from the token response / consented set) on the slot or a companion record.
2. At egress, enforce route.required_scopes ⊆ granted-scopes before the call; deny otherwise. (auth/runtime/credential_broker.py + egress_models.py.)
3. Acquirer should request per-connection granted scopes, not the blanket provider union (adapters/http_token_acquirer.py).
4. F5: HttpProviderEgress._project maps only on HTTP status; providers (Slack/Graph) return HTTP 200 {ok:false, error:invalid_auth|token_revoked|missing_scope}. Add a per-route declarative result classifier (body_ok_field + unauthorized_signals frozenset) evaluated generically in _project — invalid_auth/token_revoked -> unauthorized (drives the bounded retry), others -> denied. Data-driven, no per-provider branch. (adapters/http_egress.py + egress_models.py ProviderRoute.)

This unblocks the safe 'one Microsoft connection serves Outlook + Teams' model; until it lands, use one-connection-per-capability (least privilege).
title: security: enforce ProviderRoute.required_scopes at the egress broker + map provider {ok:false} auth errors

design: EXPERT VERDICT (strands-expert, 2026-07-01, grounded in Strands docs+SDK): Strands is STRICTLY invocation-scoped -- NO native scheduler/timer/cron/background-task primitive exists; nothing runs between invocations. Strands DOES expose completion hooks (AfterInvocationEvent, AfterMultiAgentInvocationEvent) that could fire an eval, but companion-x already centralizes completion->score in the events brick, so on-completion goes through the events brick for consistency (not a Strands Plugin). Cadence MUST live outside Strands -> the AgentRunner ClockPort (already built for Living Agents) is the idiomatic seam; avoids introducing celery-beat. Architecture lens (orchestrator call -- meta-architect subagent crashed): least-new-machinery + consistent with existing event-driven scoring.
notes:
META-ARCHITECT VERDICT (2026-07-01): APPROVED. False dichotomy resolved -- events brick is the DOWNSTREAM CONSUMER of a Strands hook, not a competing seam. WorkCompletedEmitterPlugin is a Strands HookProvider (AfterInvocationEvent) that PUBLISHES chat.turn.completed to the events bus; graph/swarm adapters emit graph.completed/swarm.completed. Pattern: Strands hook emits -> events bus -> subscription fan-out. FINALIZED APPROACH: (1) On-completion: new YAML subscription (e.g. auto-freshness-on-completion.yaml) on graph.completed + swarm.completed -> handler checks last-eval timestamp vs staleness threshold -> triggers eval if stale. No new Strands plugin -- emitters already publish. (2) Cadence: AgentRunner publishes eval.freshness.due on timer_due wake (ClockPort/auto_wake_at, fakeable via DeterministicClock) -> second YAML subscription -> SAME handler. (3) Anti-fragmentation: both triggers (completion-reactive + cadence-proactive) converge on ONE handler via the events bus. One handler, two triggers, zero new eval sinks.
IMPLEMENTER (f12817df, 2026-07-01): on-completion freshness COMPLETE + tested. freshness_handler.py (handle_freshness_check) + 3 subscriptions (graph.completed, swarm.completed, eval.freshness.due) -> freshness_dispatch; wired in dispatch.py. Staleness threshold configurable via FRESHNESS_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_S (default 3600s). No cross-brick imports (evals via invoker). Events suite 236 pass/0 fail. SCOPE DECISION: cadence EMIT (AgentRunner publishing eval.freshness.due on timer_due) DEFERRED to follow-up .5 — handler side already routes eval.freshness.due. Pending qa-tester.
title: Eval-freshness trigger (on-completion via events brick + cadence via AgentRunner ClockPort)

description: useLaunchSwarmRenderer (subagent-hooks.tsx) renders a SubagentChildRows that shows 'Waiting for run id...' when runId is null. runId comes from extractRunId(parameters, parsed) which reads result.run_id or result.workflow_run_id. spawn_swarm is a SYNC streaming tool — it yields Strands events inline and returns nothing (the generator has no final yield with a run_id dict). The useLaunchSwarmRenderer card is designed for agent_launch_swarm (the old MCP tool that returned a run_id dict). spawn_swarm never returns a result object. The problem is that both useLaunchSwarmRenderer AND useSpawnSwarmRenderer may fire for the same turn if the agent calls spawn_swarm (not agent_launch_swarm). Verify no name collision. acceptance_criteria: Only a verified gateway/policy adapter can issue usable DCAL authority; arbitrary component code and caller envelopes cannot mint or scope it. Authorization verifies source ownership and action before signature/idempotency work. Child/background tasks do not retain request authority after scope teardown. Regression tests cover each bypass.
close_reason: Removed public DCAL mint/scoping/callback authorization paths; added fail-closed authority, canonical security, and regression coverage.
description: CWE-284/CWE-863: runtime/dcal/trusted.py exports mint_trusted_envelope(), which accepts caller-created TrustedBinding and returns a valid TrustedEnvelope. Any in-process component can then pass an allow-all DcalAuthorizationPort to authorize_then() and bypass the required gateway/policy verification. ContextVar authority is also copied into child asyncio tasks, allowing a child spawned during a request to retain authority after parent reset. Fix by moving minting/scoping behind a non-public gateway verifier capability; never export it from dcal/__init__; create trusted bindings only after verified auth and source-ownership lookup; use explicit, bounded request capability propagation or spawn sanitized background tasks. Add adversarial tests for importable mint bypass, forged authorizer, and child-task retention after parent reset.
title: Security: DCAL TrustedEnvelope can be minted by arbitrary component callers

description: Timeline SSE only shows API-proxied tool calls. Root cause: instrumentation._emit() calls in-process event_bus which is isolated per process. 4. Trace-level evaluators with no trace get a FABRICATED single-span session with available_tools=[] — session_evaluator.py:36-38. tool_selection then scores a trajectory containing no tools.

Also note the degenerate-input asymmetry: every evaluator  -d The

acceptance_criteria: Adapter verified against a real local MLflow tracking store (file backend), not a MagicMock. Tests exercise the real client. Run lifecycle produces a queryable finished run with params, metrics and artifacts.
description:
Verified directly against the pinned version by introspecting signatures:

  mlflow 3.14.0
  end_run      accepts run_id = False   (status: str = FINISHED) -> None
  log_param    accepts run_id = False   (key, value, synchronous) -> Any
  log_params   accepts run_id = True
  log_metric   accepts run_id = True
  log_metrics  accepts run_id = True
  log_artifact accepts run_id = True

mlflow_adapter.py:61 calls end_run(run_id=..., status=...) and :85 calls log_param(key, value, run_id=run_id). Both raise TypeError. list_runs also raises MlflowException.

Five of seven fluent APIs do accept run_id, so a pattern that is 71 percent correct was generalized to all of them.

Two aggravating factors worth reading together, because this is the most instructive failure in the whole audit:
- The code comments assert the opposite of the truth: "# Bug fix: pass run_id so we end the intended run, not the active one" (:60) and "# Bug fix: pass run_id directly" (:83). A correct concern, fixed with an API that does not exist.
- test_mlflow_adapter.py:52 injects a MagicMock into sys.modules, and the two tests labelled "Bug A fix" / "Bug B fix" assert exactly the signatures that fail. A MagicMock accepts any kwarg, so the test could never fail. The fix was validated against a mock of its own assumption.

Every trainer wraps tracker calls in except Exception: return None, None, so the end_run failure is swallowed and runs would be created, logged, then orphaned with no linkage recorded - if the adapter were reachable at all (see sibling bead).

Process fix worth adopting from this: no adapter for a third-party service may be tested exclusively against a mock of that service.
title: ml: MLflow adapter passes run_id to fluent APIs that reject it — verified broken on pinned mlflow 3.14.0

acceptance_criteria: An explicit written architectural decision, reviewed by meta-architect, and ml-dataset-generation.md updated to match whichever way it goes. If native is ratified, the spec's reuse-only language and upstream-revision canary language must be removed rather than left contradicting the code.
description:
pyproject.toml:81 now reads: "The Agentic-Datasets git pin was removed - its stage logic is slated for native reimplementation in the dataset brick." The four frameworks were reimplemented in runtime/stages/ INCLUDING their prompts (_prompts_agentinstruct.py, _prompts_s2m.py, _prompts_apigenmt.py, _prompts_reviewinstruct.py).

This directly reverses normative spec language in ml-dataset-generation.md:
- "AgentInstruct, S2M, APIGenMT, and ReviewInstruct ... are implemented ONLY as internal DatasetStagePort adapters"
- "The factory must reuse those framework capabilities rather than reimplement their agent orchestration or data transformations."
- "it must not reimplement prompts, transformations, agent orchestration, tool selection, or fallback logic"
- "pinned to the unpublished upstream commit 26cb6833a5fec672d429efa54c17d83ee8e61b4e"

The reversal may well be defensible - the upstream repo is unpublished and unversioned, so pinning a private commit is fragile. That is not the problem. The problem is HOW it happened:

It landed inside commit 8cee07dc, "merge: reconcile local WIP with CAN taxonomy + TimeGAN work from remote". A normative architectural boundary was changed as a side effect of resolving a merge conflict, with no design note, no bead, and no meta-architect verdict. The spec still asserts the opposite today, and its status table still marks "Agentic-Datasets v2 adapters and compatibility canaries" as Complete.

Decide it deliberately, then make the spec and the code agree.
title: dataset: Agentic-Datasets upstream pin was deleted and the 4 frameworks reimplemented natively — ratify or revert

acceptance_criteria: Either the canary is deleted as meaningless, or it is replaced by something that can actually fail: golden-output fixtures for each stage, or behavioral conformance tests derived from the published technique.
description:
stage_canary.py asserts that four callables in factory.dataset.runtime.stages have parameter sets matching a hardcoded EXPECTED_STAGE_PARAMETERS dict in the same repo.

Since the upstream dependency was removed, both sides of the comparison are now first-party code. The canary checks the repo against its own hardcoded expectation. It cannot fail unless someone edits one file and not the other, and it provides zero protection against the thing it was designed for.

The spec still claims: "An import/version/signature canary fails closed if the installed VCS revision or callable parameters differ." There is no installed VCS revision anymore, so that guarantee is structurally unachievable.

Same class of problem as the strands canary in evals (see wvkvg.4): a canary that checks names rather than behavior certifies nothing.
title: dataset: stage_canary is a tautology — it cannot detect the drift it exists to catch

acceptance_criteria: At least one quality check can fail on plausible bad output and is proven to by a red-then-green test. quality_can.py either wired into the production path or deleted. Steering docs corrected. Enforcement not conditional on scenario_generation being set.
description:
The spec claims six quality checks with fail-closed enforcement. Six exist. Almost none can fail:

- record_count and schema cannot fail for typed records (they are already validated by pydantic upstream)
- duplicate_detection emits a "warn:" prefix, and base.py:143 treats warn as passing
- max_message_length fires at 100,000 characters
- role_coverage unions roles across the WHOLE dataset, so 10,000 user-only records plus one assistant record passes
- only empty_messages actually bites

Enforcement raises in exactly one place, materializer.py:47, and is guarded on request.scenario_generation is not None - so recipes without scenario generation skip enforcement entirely.

Meanwhile quality_can.py contains the genuinely meaningful checks and has ZERO production callers and ZERO tests, while .agents/steering/can-handover.md:21 marks it "Complete". That combination - real code, no callers, documented as done - is the single clearest documentation-vs-reality gap found in the audit.

A dataset brick whose stated purpose is "high quality, very good looking datasets" currently cannot detect a low-quality dataset.
title: dataset: quality gates are near-tautologies, and the meaningful ones (quality_can.py) are dead code

acceptance_criteria: For each of the four stages, either the missing mechanism is implemented, or the stage is renamed and its docstring states plainly what it does and does not do. No placeholder string may ever reach a materialized dataset. No fixture may enshrine a placeholder as expected output.
description:
Each stage is a competent 1-2 call prompt chain, but each drops the mechanism that is the technique's actual contribution. That matters because these names are how the dataset quality gets described to other people.

- agentinstruct.py: 7 static transform prompts plus an optional complexity call. No taxonomy, no suggester-editor agent pair.
- apigenmt.py:110: asks an LLM where a tool would help, then asks another LLM to HALLUCINATE the tool's output, and stamps status="completed". APIGen-MT's entire premise is execution validation against real tools. This produces training data teaching a model that fabricated tool results are real ones.
- reviewinstruct.py: the prompt text says "You are the chairman in a multi-agent review process" and there is exactly one reviewer.
- s2m.py: one JSON-array call gated on len >= 4.

None of the four can ever drop a record, so no stage can reduce dataset size - a review stage that cannot reject anything is not a review stage.

Worst concrete instance: s2m.py:73 writes the literal string "[Example would be provided here with LLM generation enabled]" into an assistant turn, and s2m.py:126-139 emits that placeholder even when use_llm=True. A golden parity fixture enshrines that string as expected output, so the test suite actively protects it.

Non-LLM paths are degenerate generally: apigenmt and reviewinstruct are pure passthroughs (via="disabled"), agentinstruct concatenates a canned suffix sentence. Any recipe run with use_llm=False produces a dataset that looks structurally valid and contains nothing.
title: dataset: native stages are shallower than the techniques they are named after

acceptance_criteria: dataset appears in MCP_INCLUDE_BRICKS, get_brick_tools(dataset) returns its tools through companion-x, and a full submit -> poll -> artifact -> manifest cycle is driven end-to-end over call_brick_tool. Same review for learning, curator and oracle.
description:
The dataset brick declares mcp_enabled: true and registers real tools (dataset_submit_generation, dataset_get_job, dataset_cancel_job, dataset_publish_scenario_pack, plus deterministic ones). But it is absent from MCP_INCLUDE_BRICKS in the companion-x server config, so get_brick_tools("dataset") returns: Unknown brick: dataset.

Verified: 29 bricks exposed, dataset is not among them. Also missing: learning, curator, oracle.

The spec status table says "Dataset MCP tools callable - Complete - All 5 tools verified end-to-end through fastmcp." That is true of the brick's own server.py and false through the MCP surface anyone actually uses. The stated goal is that an agent can drive the brick completely; today it cannot reach it at all.

acceptance_criteria: An explicit written decision to delete, or to rebuild correctly with a stated evaluation oracle. If rebuilt: 5 networks incl. supervisor, alternating G/D updates, generator sees real data, and a synthesis-quality metric independent of downstream classifier AUROC.
description:
Two separate problems. The implementation is broken, and the approach is questionable even if fixed. Decide the second question before spending effort on the first.

== 1. It is not TimeGAN, and it cannot converge ==

timegan_models.py declares only Generator and Discriminator. TimeGAN (Yoon et al. 2019) requires five networks: embedder, recovery, generator, discriminator, supervisor. The supervised loss carried by the supervisor is the paper's actual contribution. There is no autoencoder and no supervised loss here, so this is a plain sequence GAN wearing the TimeGAN name.

The training loop has no adversarial alternation - timegan.py:92-115:
  phase 1 (epochs_reconstruction): G.train(); D.eval() - only G updated, for the whole phase
  phase 2 (epochs_adversarial):    D.train(); G.eval() - only D updated, for the whole phase
So G is optimized to fool a randomly-initialized D, then D is trained to detect a frozen G. No minimax game ever runs. The phase name "reconstruction" is also wrong - nothing is reconstructed.

Additionally x_real enters the generator phase only as x_real.size(0). The generator never observes real data.

Same defects in the conditional variant.

Consequence, and why this matters more than the bug itself: can-gan-loop-report.md records "GAN Loop Not Improving - identical AUROC across iterations (0.80, 0.80, 0.80)". That is the expected behavior of this code. It was diagnosed instead as a feedback-wiring problem, and four commits went into treating it (d0574406 dual-objective loss + feedback wiring, a76f7ad5 checkpoint continuity + feedback, 0e7e3245 conditional TimeGAN, d49b80c0 correlation-based injection). Three days of tuning a loop that cannot converge by construction.

== 2. The approach is probably wrong regardless ==

a) No training signal exists for it. can-complete-work-catalog.md states the 131GB of decoded CAN is 100 percent normal driving with zero failures. A GAN learns the distribution it is shown. Trained on normal driving it can only produce normal driving; asking it for failures is asking for out-of-distribution samples, which is precisely what GANs are worst at.

b) The conditioning source is a different domain. SCANIA APS is truck air-pressure-system tabular data (60k CSV rows), not CAN frames. Transplanting its failure shapes onto decoded CAN signals is an unvalidated cross-domain transfer with no physical justification recorded.

c) There is no oracle. Judging synthesis realism requires real failures to compare against, and there are none. Downstream classifier AUROC does not measure synthesis quality - a classifier scores well by detecting generator artifacts. That is the already-documented "Challenge 3: models detect injection method" failure, restated with a more elaborate injector. Making the injector more sophisticated makes the artifact harder to see, not absent.

d) SDK-first: sdv>=1.37.0 is already a dependency and ships sequential synthesizers (PAR) plus SDMetrics quality scoring. Hand-rolling a GAN duplicates an installed framework that also provides the quality metric this work lacks.

e) The repo's own spec prefers deterministic injection. ml-dataset-generation.md specifies seeded, reproducible injection with exact semantics (ecu_timeout zeroing every decoded signal across the window, signal_freeze holding only selected signals), tracked as the P0 correctness gate python-factory-sbhyq.11. Deterministic injection is auditable, seedable, and explainable to a customer. A GAN is none of those.

== Recommendation ==

Delete TimeGAN (timegan.py, timegan_models.py, timegan_loss.py, timegan_checkpoint.py, timegan_conditional*.py - 6 files) and reallocate to sbhyq.11 deterministic physics-constrained injection.

Then reframe the modeling problem - see sibling bead on supervised-vs-anomaly framing. With abundant normal data and no failure labels, this is semi-supervised anomaly detection, not supervised classification, and Chronos-2 is already pinned and well suited to residual scoring on normal behavior.

Keep synthetic injection for PIPELINE TESTING only, never as training truth.
title: DECISION: TimeGAN is structurally broken AND probably the wrong tool — recommend deleting it

acceptance_criteria: A written framing decision. If anomaly detection is adopted: a normality model trained on real normal data, a deviation score, and a held-out validation set of REAL failure events (however small) as the only promotion oracle. Synthetic injection demoted to pipeline testing.
description:
This is the root cause behind several of the other findings, and it is a framing question rather than a bug.

Current state, from the project's own documents: 131GB of decoded CAN is 100 percent normal driving with zero failures. Every training label is therefore synthetic. can-complete-work-catalog.md already names the consequence - "Challenge 3: Models Detect Injection Method, AUROC 0.97-1.00 on synthetic data, but detecting injection not failures."

The remedy applied so far has been to make the injector more realistic (SCANIA patterns, correlated multi-signal, gradual onset/decay, conditional GAN). That reduces the artifact but cannot remove it, because the model is still trained against labels that a function in this repo invented. Reported AUROC is measuring agreement with the injector, not failure detection. This is why the numbers hover near chance on anything realistic (LightGBM 0.50-0.64, TCN 0.39-0.86) and jump when the injection is cruder.

The alternative framing uses the data that actually exists. Abundant normal data with no labeled failures is the textbook setting for semi-supervised anomaly detection:

- Fit a model of NORMAL CAN behavior on the 131GB (no labels needed).
- Score deviation from normality: forecast residuals, reconstruction error, or density.
- Alert on sustained deviation rather than classifying an injected pattern.
- Validate on a small set of REAL failure events from service records. Even a handful of true events is a valid oracle; unlimited synthetic events are not.

This fits assets already pinned and already built:
- chronos-forecasting 2.3.1 (Chronos-2) is a pretrained time-series foundation model. Forecast normal signal behavior, score residuals. Zero failure labels required. It is already wired.
- ncps 1.0.1 LTC and PatchTST are usable the same way.
- The existing windowing, decode, and profiling pipeline in the dataset brick is reusable unchanged - only the label/target semantics change.

Practical consequences if adopted:
- Removes the dependency on synthetic labels being realistic, which removes the unfalsifiable part of the current program.
- Synthetic injection stays useful for pipeline testing and for measuring detector sensitivity to KNOWN perturbations, which is a legitimate and honest use.
- The GAN becomes unnecessary (see sibling bead).
- The supervised per-CAN-ID competition results become sensitivity measurements rather than performance claims, and should be relabeled as such wherever they are reported.

Do not treat this as settled - it is a decision for the owner. But the current supervised framing cannot produce a defensible number, and no amount of model or injector work changes that.
title: DECISION: reframe CAN failure prediction as anomaly detection, not supervised classification

description:
Goal: turn Sandbox from an environment inventory into a cross-brick operational surface that shows what agents are doing inside environments and links that activity across Sandbox, Workflow, Events/Timeline, Graph, Metrics, and Evals.

Why: Metrics feels elevated because it summarizes signals coming from other bricks rather than only rendering its own records. Sandbox has the same opportunity, especially for agentic workflows like SAST, but it currently stops at environment state.

Vision:
- Sandbox becomes the operator's lens for live environment activity
- Workflow shows orchestration/run state
- Events/Timeline shows the ordered event stream
- Graph shows entities, findings, artifacts, and relationships produced by the run
- Metrics/Evals show outcome and performance signals derived from that activity

Core product outcomes:
- show which workflow run is attached to an environment
- show which agents or nodes are acting inside the environment
- show commands, artifacts, and findings produced in that environment
- show graph context and related entities/findings for that environment
- provide clean cross-tab navigation between Sandbox, Workflow, Events, Graph, Metrics, and Evals

Architecture direction:
- this is primarily a cross-brick correlation model and interaction contract, not just a UI uplift
- may require taxonomy extensions, but the main need is shared correlation IDs and shared activity semantics
- standardize correlation fields such as env_id, run_id, graph_id, target_app, agent_id, and node_id
- emit canonical events such as sandbox.provisioned, sandbox.command_executed, sandbox.file_uploaded, workflow.run_started, workflow.node_completed, and finding.created
- persist graph relationships such as WorkflowRun -> USES -> SandboxEnvironment, Agent -> EXECUTED_IN -> SandboxEnvironment, WorkflowRun -> PRODUCED -> Finding, and SandboxEnvironment -> HOSTED -> Artifact

Initial implementation slice:
- add shared correlation fields across sandbox, workflow, events, and graph
- add sandbox summary/read tools for correlated activity, not just environment state
- add a Live Activity section in Sandbox driven by events/history and keyed by env_id/run_id
- add a Graph Context drill-down in Sandbox for related entities/findings
- keep the UI minimal, elegant, and consistent with the elevated Metrics/Evals style

Acceptance shape:
- from an agentic workflow run, a user can open Sandbox and see live or recent activity for an environment
- from Sandbox, a user can identify the linked workflow run, related graph entities/findings, and recent event history
- the experience feels like one product surface rather than isolated brick tabs
- the resulting dashboard remains crisp and low-noise rather than turning into a generic graph inspector

Suggested breakdown after creation:
1. define shared correlation model and event taxonomy additions
2. instrument sandbox/workflow/events/graph with shared IDs
3. add sandbox activity summary MCP tools
4. add sandbox live activity and graph context UI
5. add metrics/evals style cross-navigation where appropriate
title: Create cross-brick sandbox activity experience

description:
Three tests in components/ui/test/factory/ui/test_canvas_paint_e2e.py fail with TypeError: '_CallbackEntry' object is not callable.

Root cause: the test's own _fire_after_tool helper (line 88-90) iterates strands' PRIVATE HookRegistry._registered_callbacks and calls each entry directly. As of the installed strands version, that dict holds _CallbackEntry dataclass wrappers (.venv/.../strands/hooks/registry.py:41,182,257) rather than bare callables, so cb(evt) raises.

Fix: read entry.callback, or better, stop touching the private attribute and drive the registry through its public dispatch API.

Pre-existing, NOT caused by bd:3jcls.3 (no file in the paint/plugin/mapper path was modified there). Verified failing independently of the action-dispatcher work. Blocks a clean 'uv run pytest components/ui/test' green run.
title: Bug: test_canvas_paint_e2e reaches into Strands private _registered_callbacks, broken by _CallbackEntry wrapper
